sections.heading: 3. Jurisdiction & Privacy
sections.body:
> _(reproduced verbatim from `legal-0_58_45-05_05_26-1200.md`; the v0.60.132 addition — the identity-free free-text search-term log — is appended as the final bullet of this section and cross-referenced in §7.)_

- **Jurisdiction:** Singapore. Bot serves SG-specific data sets and complies with Singapore-side terms (LTA / NEA data licences, HDB carpark licence, IMDA Model AI Governance Framework alignment for AI-mediated output).
- **PDPA Section 13(c) / GDPR Article 17 alignment:** users can wipe every chatId-keyed Redis entry on demand via `/forgetme`. Returns a deletion summary so the user has a record.
- **No personal data sent to third parties.** Chat IDs are sha256-hashed before being used as Redis keys for location / processing state. Telegram user IDs are visible only to the LLM providers when their APIs are called, and only as the bot's own request initiator (not as user attribution).
- **AI-mediated content disclaimers:**
  - `/hidden` results are generated by Google Gemini with Google Search grounding. Despite explicit "do not fabricate" prompt rules + post-process safeguards (e.g. `rewriteFabricatedPlaceUrls` rejects fabricated Place IDs), the model can still return inaccurate or stale facts about restaurants, opening hours, or social-media coverage. Verify before acting.
  - Tell-Gia (cuisine NL) uses Anthropic Claude to map free-text to cuisine slugs. Misclassifications happen; the user can always pick cuisines manually in the TMA.
  - `/recognised` award lists are LLM-fetched (Anthropic Claude) and grounded with web search; year-scoped and 24 h cached. Authoritative source remains the original award body's website.
- **Free-text search-term log (added v0.60.131; retention raised to 90 days v0.60.132).** The food / dish / cuisine words a user types into chat free-text or the Cuisine Mini App's "Tell me" box are recorded in Redis (`freetext:log` — a capped list of the last 5 000 entries; `freetext:log:<YYYY-MM-DD>` — per-day lists) **with no chat ID, Telegram user ID, or any other user identifier** — each entry is `{ q (search text, ≤ 80 chars), ts, src ('chat' | 'cuisine-tma'), chip (was a cuisine chip active), m (which guard/table matched, if any), n (result count) }`. It is a corpus of *what is searched*, never *who searched*. Purpose: extend the misrepresented-dish / cooking-method / dessert-drink reference tables, tune the question-shaped-query guard, and surface recurring search failures. **Not exported off-platform; sent to no third party; not covered by `/forgetme`** (there is nothing chatId-keyed to delete — by construction it holds no identity). Both the capped list and the per-day lists carry a 90-day Redis TTL refreshed on each write, so the corpus self-clears after 90 days of inactivity, consistent with the `/privacy` retention promise. An operator-only `/ftlog [N]` command (gated by `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID`, like `/ver`) dumps recent entries; a silent no-op for everyone else.

journal.title: [HDR] #152 | 12:10:00 SGT 15-05-26 | v0.60.185 — Michelin walk-through copy fix (▶ → 🔍) + page-tap diagnostic logging | 3 files, ~15 LOC | 1 PR |
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]**
  - **Copy**: the Cuisine TMA Michelin indicator said "Tap ▶ for the next batch of 12." but there is no ▶ button on the TMA — users tap the 🔍 Search button. Glyph mismatch confused the operator (and likely other users). Change ▶ → 🔍 in both EN + FR.
  - **Diagnostic logging**: operator reports "Michelin listing cannot refresh next 12 again" without enough detail to triage. Add a one-line per-tap log capturing `criteriaHash`, `seenBefore`, `pool`, `candidatesFiltered`, `appendKeys`, `didReset` so the next reproduction has Railway evidence. Real fix held until the symptom is reproduced.

- **[DELTA]**

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/App.jsx`**:
  - Line ~1209–1210: EN "Tap ▶ for the next batch of 12." → "Tap 🔍 for the next batch of 12.". FR "Touchez ▶ pour le prochain groupe de 12." → "Touchez 🔍 pour le prochain groupe de 12.". v0.60.149 comment block updated to reference 🔍 instead of ▶ for future readers.
  - Line ~155 internal comment updated to match.

  **`index.js`** — Michelin handler (`handleMichelinSearch`):
  - Inserted a `console.log` immediately before `appendSeenSet` (line ~6504) emitting `[Michelin] page chatId=… hash=… seenBefore=N pool=N candidatesFiltered=N appendKeys=N didReset=bool`. The pre-existing tap log (`[Michelin] tap …`) covers the entry side; this new log covers the exit side so Railway can correlate the two.
  - No behavioural change beyond logging.

  **`package.json`** — `0.60.184 → 0.60.185` (PATCH; copy + diagnostics, no contract change).

  **`doc/Journal/journal-0_60_185-15_05_26-1210.md`** — this entry (#152).

  **`doc/.serial-state.yml`** — `journal 151 → 152`, `commit 158 → 159`, `technical 35 → 36`; re-anchored `15-05 '26 12:10 SGT`.

  Web/cuisine rebuilt via `npm run build` (App.jsx changed).

- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**

  ```bash
  $ node --check index.js
  syntax OK
  $ npm test -- --run
   Tests  1790 passed (1790)
  $ cd web/cuisine && npm run build
   ✓ built in 1.28s
  ```

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy:
  1. Open Cuisine TMA → tap ✳️ Michelin chip → first tap returns 12 venues + indicator "📚 Curated Michelin list — N more to explore. **Tap 🔍 for the next batch of 12.**" (NOT ▶).
  2. Tap 🔍 again → next 12 venues (operator: please confirm whether or not this works on production; the bug report needs reproduction).
  3. Railway logs should now show two correlated lines per Michelin tap: `[Michelin] tap …` (entry) and `[Michelin] page …` (exit). Operator can grep `[Michelin]` to capture the seen-set timeline if the "cannot refresh" symptom appears again.

- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - **DF-80 NEW (UNRESOLVED BUG)** — "Michelin listing cannot refresh next 12 again". Reproduction details required from operator: (a) which chip / cuisine combo? (b) does this happen on the second tap, or only after the 11th tap (cycle-end)? (c) does the indicator text remain unchanged or does it disappear? (d) does the search button stay enabled? With the new diagnostic logs, the next reproduction in Railway should pin the root cause within 1–2 taps.
  - **DF-81 NEW** — Dashboard restoration: restore the 10 instruments + Lessons block from `doc/VibeCodingRecord/generate.mjs` (lines 470–485) into the new `.vibe-journal/` tabbed bundle as a `📊 Dashboard` tab. Operator approved full restoration. Scheduled for v0.60.186.
  - **DF-82 NEW** — Vibe Journal auth-hardening backlog: `timingSafeEqual` swap for the `=== want` compare at `index.js:8105` + 30/hr/IP rate-limit on the `/doc/:file` route. Operator opted to defer; not urgent given `VIBE_JOURNAL_KEY` length is the dominant factor.
  - DF-V1 → DF-V4, DF-49 / DF-50 / DF-53 / DF-55 / DF-60 → DF-79 carried.

journal.title: [HDR] #151 | 11:55:00 SGT 15-05-26 | v0.60.184 — Emoji map pins across Cuisine TMA + /app/map + /transport (bus stops + carparks) | 4 files, ~85 LOC | 1 PR |
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Operator: *"Should replace boring pins in the Google Map for specifics like 🐾 Pins for Pet Allowed or 🍮 for Dessert or ✳️ for curated Michelin list or 🅿️ car park or 🚏 Bus Stop."* Both interactive map surfaces (the Cuisine TMA's `MapPanel.jsx` and the public `/app/map` view at `public/app.js`) use Google Maps JS API `AdvancedMarkerElement` + `PinElement` — the `glyph` parameter accepts an emoji string natively, so this is a single-attribute swap per pin.

- **[DELTA]**

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/components/MapPanel.jsx`** — Cuisine TMA interactive map.

  - New top-of-file helper `pinGlyphFor(venue)` returning the priority-ordered emoji glyph (Michelin > Pet > Dessert) or `null` for the default coloured circle. Dessert detection via `DESSERT_RX = /dessert|patisserie|p[âa]tisserie|bakery|cafe|caf[ée]|ice ?cream|gelato|sweet|confection/i` so French / English / mixed-case all match.
  - Per-venue loop (line ~248): now passes `glyph: glyph || undefined` into `new PinElement(...)` and bumps `scale` from `1` → `1.15` when an emoji glyph is set (legibility on small screens against the orange/green background).
  - Behaviour unchanged for venues without a matching attribute — they render as before (plain coloured circle).

  **`public/app.js`** — public `/app/map` view (DOM-rendered AdvancedMarker).

  - New `pinGlyphFor(venue)` mirrors the TMA helper and adds `kind: 'busStop'` → `🚏` and `kind: 'carPark'` → `🅿️` for the /transport bus-stop and /carpark map surfaces (those payloads don't have michelinCategory / allowsDogs / restaurantType — they're a distinct kind entirely).
  - `makePinContent(num, name, isUser, venue)` — added the `venue` parameter; when a glyph applies, the inner `<span class="num">` shows the emoji instead of the numeric index.
  - `renderVenues` call site (line ~143) updated to pass `v` into `makePinContent`.

  **`maps-url.js`** — slim payload preservation.

  - `buildMapHashUrl`'s `buildSlim` (around line 188) was previously dropping every venue attribute except name / placeId / area / lat / lng / vibe / url / arrivals / lines. The TMA's deep-link round-trip via `/app/map#venues=<base64>` therefore arrived at the public view with NO glyph metadata. Now preserves `michelinCategory`, `allowsDogs`, `restaurantType`, and `kind` when present so the `/app/map` `pinGlyphFor()` has the inputs it needs.

  **`index.js`** — set the `kind` field at the two transport-map slim sites.

  - Bus-stop slim builder (line ~3013, the `slim.push(...)` for nearest bus stops) now includes `kind: 'busStop'`.
  - Carpark map (line ~3465, `carparksWithName` map): adds `kind: 'carPark'`.
  - These are the two points where /transport's bus-stop list and /carpark's nearest-5 list construct the multi-pin map payload; without the `kind` tag, the maps-url `buildSlim` had nothing to preserve and the public/app.js `pinGlyphFor()` couldn't pick the right emoji.

  **`package.json`** — `0.60.183 → 0.60.184` (PATCH; cosmetic map glyph; no contract change).

  **`doc/Journal/journal-0_60_184-15_05_26-1155.md`** — this entry (#151).

  **`doc/.serial-state.yml`** — `journal 150 → 151`, `commit 157 → 158`, `feature 39 → 40`; re-anchored `15-05 '26 11:55 SGT`.

  Web/cuisine rebuilt via `cd web/cuisine && npm run build` (MapPanel.jsx changed).

- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**

  ```bash
  $ node --check index.js && node --check public/app.js && node --check maps-url.js
  syntax OK
  $ npm test -- --run
   Tests  1790 passed (1790)
  $ cd web/cuisine && npm run build
   ✓ built in 1.26s
  ```

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy. No server-side data migration. Behavioural change is purely cosmetic (pin glyph). Falls back gracefully — venues without matching attributes still render as the legacy coloured-circle pin.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy:
  1. **Cuisine TMA** → open map panel. Expected glyphs on the AdvancedMarker pins:
     - Michelin-listed venue (✳️ category set) → **✳️**
     - Pet-allowed venue (allowsDogs=true) → **🐾**
     - Dessert / bakery / cafe / patisserie / gelato venue (restaurantType matches DESSERT_RX) → **🍮**
     - Other venues → plain coloured circle (orange when focused, green otherwise) — unchanged

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]**
  - **Item 5**: `/s` (technique fan-out, nation-iconic fan-out, cooking-method fan-out, free-text single-query) was rendering venues WITHOUT the `🍽️ <cuisine type>` row that the Cuisine TMA's ResultCard already shows. Root cause: `formatTechniqueVenueBlock` (index.js:5208) skipped `venue.restaurantType` entirely, and the TMA's Copy-All `enriched` payload didn't ship `restaurantType` to the server. Restore both.

When the user's home country differs from the venue's, append the converted-to-device-currency equivalent in parens to 2 decimal places, e.g. `S$25–40 (US$18.50–29.60)`. FX via the free **Frankfurter API** (ECB-sourced, daily), cached in Redis for 12 h. Graceful degradation when FX unreachable.

- **[DELTA]**

  **`pipeline.js`** — Places New API field-mask + normalisation extensions.

  - `DISCOVER_FIELD_MASK` (line ~879): added `places.priceRange` (numeric range object: `{ startPrice:{ currencyCode, units, nanos }, endPrice:{…} }`) and `places.addressComponents` (used to extract the venue's ISO-3166 country code). Both are paid fields in the New API — marginal per-request cost documented below.
  - New helpers `normalisePriceRange(p)` and `extractCountryCode(addressComponents)` near `priceLevelToInt`. The former returns `{ currencyCode, start, end }` or `null`; the latter scans `addressComponents[]` for the `'country'`-typed component and returns the `shortText` (alpha-2).
  - Venue-construction block (~line 1112): `priceRange: normalisePriceRange(p.priceRange)`, `country: extractCountryCode(p.addressComponents)` added to the returned venue object.

  **`currency-format.js`** (NEW, ~140 LOC) — the formatter.

  - `COUNTRY_PREFIX` map: operator-specified `SG → S$`, `MY → M$`, plus `US$ / C$ / HK$ / NT$ / A$ / NZ$ / ¥ / ₩ / ฿ / ₫ / Rp / ₱ / ₹ / £ / € / CHF` covering SEA + global majors. EU-zone codes (DE, FR, IT, …) all → `€`.
  - `CURRENCY_PREFIX` map keyed by ISO-4217 for the secondary lookup. Fallback: `"<CODE> "`.
  - `COUNTRY_TO_CURRENCY` for FX-rate lookup (country → ISO-4217).
  - `fetchFxRate(from, to, redis)` — Frankfurter API call (`api.frankfurter.app/latest?from=&to=`), 8 s `AbortSignal.timeout`, Redis cache at `fx:<from>:<to>` with 12-hour TTL, `null` on any failure. Same-currency short-circuits to `1.0` without hitting the network.
  - `formatPriceRangeForVenue(priceRange, venueCountry, userCountry, redis)` — orchestrates: pick venue prefix → format `<prefix><start>–<end>` (or single bound) → if cross-border, fetch FX and append `(<userPrefix>start–end)` to 2 dp. Returns `null` when `priceRange` is unusable; returns the native-only string when FX fails or when same-country/unknown-user. **Caller drops the line** when this returns `null`.

  **`index.js`** — pre-resolution + render insertion.

  - New helpers near `reverseGeocodeAddress`:
    - `resolveUserCountry(chatId)` — Redis-cached at `user:<chatId>:country` (30 day TTL); on miss, reverse-geocodes the user's cached share-pin location with `result_type=country`; defaults to `'SG'` (the app's home market).
    - `enrichPriceRangeDisplay(chatId, venues)` — calls `formatPriceRangeForVenue` per venue, stashes the result on `venue.priceRangeDisplay`. Runs alongside `enrichTravelTimes` so the downstream `formatVenueBlock` + `formatTechniqueVenueBlock` stay synchronous.
  - Five call sites instrumented (matched 1:1 with the `enrichTravelTimes` call pattern, same try/catch shape):
    - free-text single-query (line ~5054)
    - `runTechniqueFanOut` (line ~5568) — drives `/s <technique>`
    - `runNationIconicFanOut` (line ~5684) — drives `/s <iconic dish>`
    - cooking-method fan-out (line ~5800)
    - `/api/cuisine/search` (line ~10404) — drives the Cuisine TMA
  - `formatTechniqueVenueBlock` (line ~5208): added `if (venue.restaurantType) lines.push(\`🍽️ \${vt.escapeHtmlForTelegram(venue.restaurantType)}\`)` after the bold name (mirrors `formatVenueBlock` at venue-templates.js:191 — the gap that hid the cuisine-nationality chip from `/s` results). Also added `vt.formatPriceAndPetLine(venue, { lang })` push just before `vt.formatTravelLine(venue)`.

  **`venue-templates.js`** — new helper + stats-row trim.

  - New `formatPriceAndPetLine(p, { lang })` (exported). Reads `p.priceRangeDisplay` (pre-resolved string) and `p.allowsDogs`; joins with ` · `; returns `null` when neither contributes. The 🐾 segment: EN `🐾 Pet allowed` / FR `🐾 Animaux autorisés`.

Stats row now carries rating · crowd · [distance] only — the price slot moved to its own dedicated line via `formatPriceAndPetLine`. The change cascaded into three failing test assertions in `__tests__/venue-templates.test.js`, which were updated to reflect the new stats-row shape.

journal.title: [HDR] #146 | 10:05:00 SGT 15-05-26 | v0.60.179 petFriendly filter: tighten strict-only — drop "< 3 → keep all" fallback; accept allowsDogs=true OR pet-friendly-named only | 3 files, ~20 LOC net | 1 PR |
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** v0.60.165's design choice was: post-filter `v.allowsDogs === true`, and **if strict yields < 3 venues, keep the full text-query-biased pool** (since Places' `allowsDogs` is sparsely populated outside the densest SG areas). Operator's bug report shows the fallback is too generous: venues like "Tiong Bahru Bakery", "Zorba The Greek Taverna", "Boomarang Bistro" surface alongside the two genuinely pet-friendly ones ("CALI Rochester Park – Pet-Friendly Restaurant & Bar", "The Garden Slug Family Restaurant (Pet-Friendly Seating Available)"). Real-world consequence: users show up with their dogs and get refused. This fix prioritises **accuracy over result count**.

- **[DELTA]**

  **`index.js`** (~line 9846) — `petFriendly` post-filter rewritten:

  *Before* (v0.60.165 → v0.60.178):
  ```js
  if (filters.petFriendly && venues.length > 0) {
    const strictPet = venues.filter((v) => v.allowsDogs === true);
    if (strictPet.length >= 3) {
      venues = strictPet;
    }
    // else: KEEP ALL — the bug. Text-query bias surfaces any "pet friendly"
    // mention in reviews / name as a hit, including generic cafes.
  }
  ```

  *After* (v0.60.179):
  ```js
  if (filters.petFriendly && venues.length > 0) {
    const PET_NAME_RX = /\bpet[-\s]?friendly\b|\bdog[-\s]?friendly\b|\bpet[-\s]?allowed\b|\bpets?\s+welcome\b|\bdogs?\s+welcome\b/i;
    venues = venues.filter((v) =>
      v.allowsDogs === true ||
      PET_NAME_RX.test(v.name || '')
    );
  }
  ```

  - Drops the count threshold entirely. Strict-only: a venue passes iff Google flagged `allowsDogs === true` OR the venue's name contains an explicit pet-friendly signal (covers "CALI Rochester Park – Pet-Friendly Restaurant & Bar" + "The Garden Slug Family Restaurant (Pet-Friendly Seating Available)" + similar).
  - If zero verified venues, the existing v0.60.157 zero-results CTA in the TMA surfaces — better than showing inaccurate matches.
  - The upstream "pet friendly" cuisine-query modifier (line ~9364) stays — it still helps Places' fuzzy text ranking surface candidate venues, but only verified ones pass this post-filter.
  - Log line updated to break down the count: `kept N/M (allowsDogs=true: X, pet-friendly-named: Y)`.

  **`package.json`** — `0.60.178 → 0.60.179` (PATCH hotfix).

  **`doc/Journal/journal-0_60_179-15_05_26-1005.md`** — this entry (#146).

  **`doc/.serial-state.yml`** — `journal 145 → 146`, `commit 152 → 153`; re-anchored `15-05 '26 10:05 SGT`.

- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**

  ```bash
  $ node --check index.js
  syntax OK
  $ npm test -- --run
   Tests  1769 passed (1769)
  ```

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy. No client change required.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy reproduction:
  - Cuisine TMA → 🐾 Pet allowed ON → Search.
  - Railway log: `[Cuisine-Search] petFriendly strict (v0.60.179): kept N/M (allowsDogs=true: X, pet-friendly-named: Y)`.
  - Result list should be SMALLER and only contain venues that either Google tagged or whose names explicitly mention pet-friendliness.
  - If the list comes back zero / very small, the v0.60.157 zero-results CTA fires — that's the design (accuracy > count).

- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - **DF-67 NEW** — operator-curated allow-list of known pet-friendly SG venues (a `data/Pet Friendly Eateries.MD` table) that the post-filter can also accept. Catches venues whose Google data is missing AND whose name doesn't include the signal. Defer until operator confirms the false-negative rate is meaningful.

  if (count === 1) await redis.expire(rlKey, windowSec);
  if (count > cap) return res.status(429).json({ error: 'rate_limited', endpoint, retryAfterSec });

The Places text query becomes `"pet friendly <cuisine> restaurant"`, biasing Google's text matcher toward review mentions of pet-friendliness even when `allowsDogs` is null (sparser in JB / MY).

  **`index.js` post-filter (`~line 9760`)** — strict mode + text-query fallback:

  if (filters.petFriendly && venues.length > 0) {
    const strictPet = venues.filter((v) => v.allowsDogs === true);
    if (strictPet.length >= 3) {

    }
    // else: drop the strict filter, keep the text-query-biased pool
  }
  ```

New logic: `searchCenter = isJB ? (insideSG ? JB_CBD : { lat, lng }) : { lat, lng }`. The JB_CBD fallback now only fires when the supplied lat/lng is inside SG (proof the user toggled JB but their GPS still reports SG → no explicit pick); outside SG (Pontian, Desaru, etc.) → trust the pick.

Word-boundary keeps "Johor Bahru" matching (it contains "Johor") AND covers Pontian / Desaru / Kulai / Mersing / Muar / Batu Pahat / Iskandar Puteri / Kota Tinggi addresses (all read "<District>, Johor, Malaysia").      - Chef Kang's Noodle House: `🍴 Try · Wanton mee` / `Char siew wanton mee · Dumpling noodle` (substring duplicate)
     - Boon Tong Kee Restaurant: `🍴 Try · Hainanese chicken rice` / `Or ni · Roast chicken` (no dupe — confirms not all entries trigger)

  *"both errors were earlier PR. investigate, double check, code audit"*. Log: `https://github.com/ang-kl/gia/blob/main/log/Depoly_1815_14-May.MD`.

- **[DELTA]**

  **`index.js` `/api/cuisine/copy-all` (~line 7969-7988)** — Issue 1 root cause: Telegram caps single messages at 4096 chars. The v0.59.29 cap of 12 venues was sized for the pre-Michelin-enrichment era; the v0.60.147 + v0.60.153 enrichment added `dishes` (3 lines) + `recentReview` blockquote per Michelin venue, pushing each block to ~300-400 chars. 12 × 350 + header ≈ 4250 chars → breaches the 4096 limit on Bib Gourmand-heavy combos. The v0.60.145 plain-text retry strips HTML tags but doesn't shorten the body (HTML overhead is < 5% of total length), so the retry also hits the same ceiling. Operator log line proves it:

  ```
  [Cuisine] copy-all sendMessage failed (HTML mode): Bad Request: message is too long
  [Cuisine] copy-all sendMessage retry failed (plain): Bad Request: message is too long
  [VLOG-CLIENT 313940231] {"kind":"fetch","method":"POST","url":"/api/cuisine/copy-all","ms":1039,"ok":false,"error":"HTTP 500"}
  ```

  Fix: when `body.length > MAX_CHARS` (3800 — 4096 with safety margin for Telegram entity overhead), pack the venue blocks into N chunks via a greedy bin-packing algorithm (`packBlocksIntoChunks` — local helper). Each chunk gets a header `Picks (i/N)` so the user sees pagination. Inline keyboard (the map button) rides on the LAST chunk so it visually lands at the bottom of the message stack (after the user has scrolled past all venues). Plain-text retry path uses the same chunking helper so the fallback also splits correctly.

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/components/ResultCard.jsx` (~line 153-185)** — Issue 2 root cause: the v0.60.159 dedup filter at line 165 was `venue.dishes.filter((d) => norm(d) && norm(d) !== norm(primaryDish))` — exact-match equality only. Substring-related dishes ("wanton mee" ⊂ "char siew wanton mee") read as duplicates to the user but pass the filter. v0.60.159 caught the operator's prior screenshot (Cheok Kee + Hong Kong Yummy Soup, where signature dish exactly equalled `dishes[0]`); the new screenshot's variant case ("wanton mee" is a substring of `dishes[0]`) slipped through.

  Fix: tighten the predicate to drop any rest entry where (a) it equals primary (existing exact check, retained), OR (b) `n.includes(primaryNorm)` (the dish name is a more specific version, e.g. "Char siew wanton mee" contains "Wanton mee"), OR (c) `primaryNorm.includes(n)` (the dish name is a less specific umbrella, e.g. primary "Hainanese chicken rice" includes rest entry "chicken rice"). Plus dedup WITHIN the rest list (a `Set` of normalised entries) so two LLM-narrated names that normalise the same don't both render.

  Risk audit: the substring check could over-filter in edge cases like primary "Sashimi" + rest "Salmon sashimi" (legitimately distinct preparations). Operator preference per the screenshot is clearly "no apparent duplicates", so the slightly aggressive filter is the right trade-off — better to under-show than to read as a typo. If a future screenshot shows under-filtering on a legitimately-distinct pair, add a min-word-count guard (only substring-match when primary is ≥ 2 words).

  **`package.json`** — `0.60.162 → 0.60.163` (PATCH — two bug fixes).

  **`doc/Journal/journal-0_60_163-14_05_26-1830.md`** — this entry (#129).

  **`doc/.serial-state.yml`** — `journal 128 → 129`, `commit 133 → 134`; re-anchored to `14-05 '26 18:30 SGT` (live-fetched via `date '+%H:%M %Z'` → 10:26 UTC → 18:26 SGT, rounded to 18:30 for the round-quarter anchor; ~90 min after v0.60.162's 17:00 anchor).

- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**

  ```bash
  $ node --check index.js
  syntax OK
  $ npm test -- --run
   Test Files  56 passed (56)
        Tests  1740 passed (1740)        # unchanged — copy-all is integration-tested behaviourally
                                          # (relies on bot.sendMessage + Telegram-side validation);
                                          # the chunker helper + ResultCard substring dedup both
                                          # have small pure-function surfaces that could be
                                          # unit-tested in a follow-up (DF-45).
  $ (cd web/cuisine && npm run build)
   ✓ 65 modules transformed.
   ✓ built in 2.87s
  ```

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy after squash-merge.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy verification matrix (Telegram, owner chatId 313940231, with `/log on`):

  - **Fix 1 — copy-all chunking**:
    - Cold-mount Cuisine TMA → Michelin chip → 🔍 Search → 12 venues. Tap `📋 Copy all` button at top of result list.
    - Expect: NO modal "Couldn't send to chat" toast. Telegram chat receives 2 messages: `Picks (1/2)` with venues 1-N, then `Picks (2/2)` with venues N+1-12 + the inline `🗺️ View all on map` keyboard. Both messages render the venue blocks in the same HTML format as before.
    - Railway logs: `[Cuisine] copy-all sendMessage failed` should NOT fire (chunking path runs first and succeeds).
    - Edge case: small result sets (e.g. 3 venues, total body < 3800 chars) should still send as a single message (chunker is no-op).

  - **Fix 2 — ResultCard substring dedup**:
    - Cold-mount Cuisine TMA → Michelin chip → 🔍 Search → look at Chef Kang's Noodle House (or any Bib Gourmand stall whose curated dishes share a substring).
    - Expect: `🍴 Try · Wanton mee` line is present. Rest list below shows `Dumpling noodle` only — `Char siew wanton mee` is filtered (substring match). Boon Tong Kee should still show its full `Or ni · Roast chicken` rest list (no substring overlap with "Hainanese chicken rice").
    - Edge case: if operator finds a legitimate distinct pair being filtered (e.g. "Sashimi" + "Salmon sashimi"), come back and add a min-word-count guard.

- **[KNOWN GAPS]**

  - **DF-45** — pure-function unit tests for `packBlocksIntoChunks` (greedy bin-packer) and the ResultCard substring-dedup predicate. Both are testable in isolation (no Redis / no React tree). Logged for the next quiet pass; manual smoke matrix above is the primary check.

  - **DF-46** — the chunker doesn't try to split a SINGLE block whose length alone exceeds MAX_CHARS. If a single venue's full enrichment body ever exceeds 3800 chars (currently bounded at ~400-500 for Michelin), the chunker would still produce a single chunk that breaches the cap and the plain-text retry would also fail. Defensive truncation per-block is a follow-up; the current per-block ceiling (~500 chars per Michelin venue with all enrichment) is well under MAX_CHARS so this is theoretical for now.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Operator (verbatim, two questions):

  1. *"Cuisine TMA / Issue: Search Criteria result / Specify: Michelin List — Michelin Search, Are you search from 3 stars until the last of Bib Gourmand? Double-check. don't have to amend code yet"*
  2. *"When I am tap back more than one cuisine + Michelin, it list once and then crash. See log https://github.com/ang-kl/gia/blob/main/log/Deploy_Log_14_May.MD"*

- **[DELTA]**

  **Q1 — verified, no code change.** Per the operator's instruction, the Michelin tier walk was confirmed by inspecting the deploy log and the source. `michelin-2025.js:196` declares the catalogue as `[...STARS_THREE, ...STARS_TWO, ...STARS_ONE, ...BIB_GOURMAND]` (2 + 7 + 32 + 89 = 130 entries). `index.js:5732,5788-5789` enforces `TIER_ORDER` on starred entries; Bib Gourmand is shuffled per-tap for breadth. The seen-set progression `12 → 24 → 36 → … → 120 → exhausted/reset → 12 → 24 → …` in the deploy log (lines around 08:25 → 08:31) shows the full walk works as designed. Recorded in this entry for the audit trail.

  **Q2 — two coupled fixes in `index.js handleMichelinSearch`:**

  - **Fix A — dedup-key inflation (`index.js` ~5903 + ~5979 + ~6140)**
    - Removed the parallel `const newDedupKeys = []` accumulator at `~5903`.
    - Inside the Places-resolve loop (`~5979`), moved the dedup-key derivation onto each venue object as `venue.michelinDedupKey = `${entry.name}|${entry.address || ''}`.toLowerCase()` (set BEFORE the `venues.push(venue)`).
    - At the seen-set append (`~6140`), replaced `await appendSeenSet(csChatId, criteriaHash, newDedupKeys)` with `const postFilterDedupKeys = filteredVenues.map((v) => v.michelinDedupKey).filter(Boolean); await appendSeenSet(csChatId, criteriaHash, postFilterDedupKeys);`. Only venues that survived the cuisine + vegetarian + halal + price post-filters get counted as "seen".
    - Scrub `delete v.michelinDedupKey` on `filteredVenues` before the response leaves the handler — clients don't need the internal-only field.
    - The v0.60.44 justification comment at `~6130` was kept (verbatim, per AU-7) and an explanatory v0.60.162 block appended.

  - **Fix B — honor `req.body?.resetSeen` (`index.js` ~5696, right before `const seen = await readSeenSet(…)`)**
    - Inserted `if (req.body?.resetSeen === true && csChatId) { await resetSeenSet(csChatId, criteriaHash); console.log(`[Michelin] resetSeen honoured chatId=${csChatId} hash=${String(criteriaHash).slice(0, 8)}`); }`.
    - The v0.60.157 client-side zero-results auto-retry now actually clears the Michelin handler's seen-set on the second-attempt request, so a combo that returned 0 on tap N gets a fresh slate on the auto-retry instead of seeing the same stale dedup state.

  **`doc/Journal/journal-0_60_162-14_05_26-1700.md`** — this entry (#128).

- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**

  ```bash
  $ node --check index.js
  syntax OK
  $ npm test -- --run
   Test Files  56 passed (56)
        Tests  1740 passed (1740)        # unchanged — handler refactor; no pure-function test surface
                                          # added. DF-43 filed for a future fixture-based test that pins
                                          # the post-filter dedup invariant.
  ```

  No `web/` changes — skip the TMA build per `gia-preflight`.

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy after squash-merge.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy verification matrix (Telegram, owner chatId 313940231, with `/log on` to surface VLOG lines):

  - **Fix A — Michelin + European combo**:
    - Close + re-open Cuisine TMA (v0.60.155 mount-wipe clears `cuisine:seen:<chatId>:*`).
    - Pick Michelin chip + European chip → 🔍 Search.
    - Expect tap 1: `[Michelin] tap chatId=… hash=… seen=0 combo=[european]` → `michelin-exit venues=11 …`.
    - Tap 🔍 Search again. Expect: `[Michelin] tap … seen=11 combo=[european]` (**11, not 12** — Fix A working).
    - If pool exhausted (likely — only 11 entries match strictly): `michelin-exit venues=0 exhausted=true`. The v0.60.157 auto-retry fires.

  - **Fix B — auto-retry reaches Michelin**:
    - On the second-tap zero, observe the next log lines: `[Michelin] resetSeen honoured chatId=… hash=…` (Fix B), then `[Michelin] tap … seen=0 combo=[european]`, then `michelin-exit venues=11 …`. The user sees the SAME 11 entries again (consistent with tap 1) instead of an empty list.
    - If `resetSeen=true` ALSO returns 0 (impossible combo), the v0.60.157 zero-results CTA panel (`🔄 Reset filters & retry` + auto-opened criteria builder) surfaces as before — unchanged.

  - **Regression: solo Michelin tier walk (Q1)**:
    - Pick Michelin alone (no combo) → 🔍 Search. Expect the same `seen=12 → 24 → 36 → … → 120 → exhausted/reset → 12` progression as the v0.60.155+ logs. Fix A doesn't change solo behaviour (solo Michelin doesn't trigger the combo post-filter at `index.js:5990 (if otherCuisineSlugs.length > 0)`), so `filteredVenues === venues` on the solo path — identical 12-keys-per-tap append.

  - **Regression: cuisine-chip path (non-Michelin)**:
    - Pick any non-Michelin cuisine + run Search. Should be unaffected — the changes are scoped to `handleMichelinSearch` only.

- **[KNOWN GAPS]**

  - **DF-43 — Fixture-based unit test for the post-filter dedup invariant.** Would need a redis-stub fixture + a small Michelin handler harness. Logged for a quiet pass; manual smoke matrix above is the primary check.

  - **Strict-cuisine post-filter zero-out behaviour unchanged.** The v0.60.18 comment at `index.js:6060` (*"returning empty rather than wrong cuisine"*) remains intentional — if the operator wants a softer fallback ("show Michelin in adjacent cuisines when the strict combo zeros out"), that's a separate design decision and a separate PR.

  - **DF-44 — Client-side perception of "list once then empty"** — even with Fix A + Fix B, after the user genuinely exhausts a small combo pool (e.g. all 11 European-Michelin venues shown once), subsequent taps will surface the v0.60.157 CTA. The CTA copy is *"No matches even after a fresh search. Try widening your criteria above, or tap below to reset filters and try again."* For the Michelin combo case specifically, a clearer message like *"You've seen all 11 Michelin venues matching European cuisine — change criteria or tap below to start over"* would land better. Logged for a follow-up if the operator finds the current copy still confusing.

journal.title: [HDR] #127 | 16:15:00 SGT 14-05-26 | v0.60.161 /log v2: extend the existing user-facing trace toggle to also drive server-side Railway logging + TMA client telemetry | n/a kb | 1 PR
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Operator: *"create a log command to toggle on/off logging results send to and fro server to client, including timing, ttl, errors. do you think is possible"*

  Answered: yes, possible. Asked two clarifying questions via `AskUserQuestion`:
  - **/log scope** → operator picked **B: Server + client (full telemetry)**.
  - **TTL meaning** → operator picked **Both** (Redis key TTLs + outbound HTTP cache headers).

  Server-side instrumentation, client-side telemetry, and Redis-key-TTL surfacing are in this PR. Outbound HTTP cache headers are deferred to a follow-up (DF-40).

- **[DELTA]**

  **`verbose-log.js` extended (v0.30.4 → v0.60.161)** — preserved all existing exports (`enable`, `disable`, `isEnabled`, `say`, `TTL_S`). Added:
  - **`isOn(redis, chatId)`** — cached read (5-s in-process cache via `_cache` Map). The cache is the price gate: without it, every instrumentation call would pay one Redis GET, doubling per-request Redis traffic when verbose is OFF (cache returns false fast) AND when ON (cache returns true fast).
  - **`status(redis, chatId)`** — `{ on, ttlSeconds }` for the `/log status` reply.
  - **`vlog(chatId, payload)`** — direct emit (caller is expected to have gated on `isOn`).
  - **`vlogIf(redis, chatId, payload)`** — gate-and-emit one-shot.
  - **`vlogTtl(redis, chatId, key)`** — looks up `redis.ttl(key)` and emits `{ kind:'redis-ttl', key, ttl }`.
  - **`vlogTime(redis, chatId, label, fn)`** — wraps an async block with start/end timing; always runs the block, only emits when verbose is on; catches + re-throws so caller semantics are unchanged.
  - **`vlogHttp(redis, chatId, label, axiosResponse)`** — extracts `cache-control` / `expires` / `age` / `content-length` headers; not wired at any call site in this PR (DF-40).
  - `enable` / `disable` now invalidate the in-process cache so a fresh `/log on` is visible to the next vlog call immediately (without waiting up to 5s for the cache entry to expire).

  **`index.js` `/log` command (~line 1619)** — same `bot.onText` handler; messaging updated to surface the three new log surfaces the toggle now drives:

  ```
  🔍 Verbose mode ON (24 h auto-off).

  • 🔍 step …   chat messages for NL pipeline runs
  • [VLOG <chatId>] …          Railway logs for /api/cuisine/* + Michelin handler (timing, Redis TTLs, HTTP cache)
  • [VLOG-CLIENT <chatId>] …   Railway logs for Cuisine TMA fetch timing + window errors

  Send /log off to disable, /log status to check TTL remaining.
  ```

  `/log status` now uses the new `status()` helper to surface `~N min remaining` from the Redis TTL.

  **`index.js` new endpoint `/api/vlog` (~line 8030)** — TMA-side telemetry sink. Gates: valid initData → chatId resolved → `isOn(redis, chatId) === true`. Emits `[VLOG-CLIENT <chatId>] {…}` to Railway logs. Caps payload at 4 KB (`String.length > 4096 ? … '…[truncated]'`) so a runaway client can't flood Railway logs. Silent reject (200 ok:false) on any gate fail — the client should not behave differently based on whether the operator has verbose on/off.

  **`index.js` `/api/cuisine/search` instrumented (~line 8780)** — at entry, `vlog.vlogIf` emits `{ kind:'cuisine-search-incoming', lat, lng, cuisines, filters, prices, region, radius, freeTextLen, resetSeen, lang }`. At exit, `vlog.vlogTtl` on `cuisine:session-meta:<chatId>` + `cuisine:session-seen:<chatId>`, then `vlog.vlog` with `{ kind:'cuisine-search-exit', ms, venues, exhausted, sessionFull, pageStackDepth, cached }`. The response body carries `_vlog: true` when verbose is on for that chatId so the TMA can flip its client shim. Error path also emits `{ kind:'cuisine-search-error', error, stack }` (top 6 stack frames).

  **`index.js` `/api/cuisine/copy-one` (~line 8069) + `/api/cuisine/copy-all` (~line 7813)** — entry/exit/error vlog blocks mirroring the search path. Captures `placeId`, `nameLen`, body bytes, `count`, `ms`. The existing v0.60.145 / v0.60.156 plain-text retry markers (`console.warn('[Cuisine] copy-one sendMessage failed (HTML mode)…')`) already exist as ungated warns; left as-is so they show up regardless of `/log` state.

  **`index.js` `handleMichelinSearch` (~line 5692)** — at entry (right after the existing `[Michelin] tap …` line), `vlog.vlogIf` emits `{ kind:'michelin-incoming', hash, seen, combo, isJB, freeTextLen, radius }` + `vlog.vlogTtl` on `cuisine:seen:<chatId>:<criteriaHash>`. At exit (right before the final `res.json`), captures `{ kind:'michelin-exit', ms, handlerMs, cacheHits, cacheMisses, venues, exhausted, reset, remaining }`. The response also carries `_vlog: true` when on. The early-exit "Michelin SG-only" path for JB region also tags `_vlog`.

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/vlog.js`** — new client-side module. Exports:
  - `setEnabled(on)` / `isEnabled()` — module-level boolean (not React state).
  - `noteServerHint(response)` — inspects `response._vlog === true` and flips on. Called from `lib/api.js` after every fetch.
  - `report(payload)` — fire-and-forget POST to `/api/vlog`. Uses `navigator.sendBeacon` when available (survives page-unload, perfect for error reports), falls back to `fetch({ keepalive: true })`.
  - `timed(label, fn)` — convenience wrapper for async with start/end timing.
  - `installGlobalHandlers()` — idempotent install of `window.addEventListener('error', …)` + `unhandledrejection`. Both serialize the first 4 stack frames to keep the payload compact.

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/api.js`** — `postJson` + `getJson` both wrapped with timing + `vlog.noteServerHint(json)` + `vlog.report({ kind:'fetch', method, url, ms, ok })` on success/failure. No new endpoints; the existing public helpers (`fetchCatalogue`, `searchCuisine`, `nlQuery`, `warmStart`, `startSession`, etc.) inherit the instrumentation transparently.

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/App.jsx`** — on mount, dynamically imports `./lib/vlog.js` and calls `installGlobalHandlers()`. Dynamic import keeps the vlog module out of the critical-path bundle.

  **`package.json`** — `0.60.160 → 0.60.161` (PATCH — additive instrumentation, no API contract change for non-owner chats).

  **`doc/Journal/journal-0_60_161-14_05_26-1615.md`** — this entry (#127).

  **`doc/.serial-state.yml`** — `journal 126 → 127`, `commit 131 → 132`; re-anchored to `14-05 '26 16:15 SGT` (live-fetched via `date '+%H:%M %Z'` → 08:13 UTC → 16:13 SGT, rounded to 16:15 for the round-quarter anchor).

- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**

  ```bash
  $ node --check index.js && node --check verbose-log.js
  syntax OK
  $ npm test -- --run
   Test Files  56 passed (56)
        Tests  1740 passed (1740)        # unchanged — verbose-log surface tests are covered by
                                          # the existing chat-trace path; new vlog* helpers are
                                          # behaviour-only (no pure-function unit candidates).
                                          # DF-41 filed for a future small test that pins the
                                          # 5-s cache + invalidate-on-enable/disable behaviour.
  $ (cd web/cuisine && npm run build)
   ✓ 65 modules transformed.
   ✓ built in 2.65s
  ```

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy after squash-merge.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy verification (operator, owner-only chatId):

  - **`/log status`** (before enabling) → expect `🔍 Verbose mode is currently OFF.`
  - **`/log on`** → expect 3-bullet enable message (the v0.60.161 copy). Open Railway logs, filter on `VLOG`.
  - **Cuisine TMA → 🔍 Search** (any criteria) → expect:
    - `[VLOG <chatId>] {"kind":"cuisine-search-incoming",…}` once.
    - `[VLOG <chatId>] {"kind":"redis-ttl","key":"cuisine:session-meta:<chatId>","ttl":<n>}` once.
    - `[VLOG <chatId>] {"kind":"cuisine-search-exit","ms":<n>,"venues":<n>,…}` once.
    - `[VLOG-CLIENT <chatId>] {"kind":"fetch","method":"POST","url":"/api/cuisine/search","ms":<n>,"ok":true}` once (TMA-side timing).
  - **Cuisine TMA → Michelin chip → 🔍 Search** → expect a `[VLOG <chatId>] {"kind":"michelin-incoming",…}` + `michelin-exit` pair with `handlerMs`, `cacheHits`, `cacheMisses`, `remaining` etc.
  - **Cuisine TMA → per-card 📋 Copy** → `[VLOG <chatId>] {"kind":"copy-one-incoming",…}` + `copy-one-exit` pair.
  - **Cuisine TMA → 📋 Copy all** → `copy-all-incoming` + `copy-all-exit` pair.
  - **Forced error**: temporarily change the TMA's `/api/cuisine/search` URL to a 404 path (DevTools) → expect a `[VLOG-CLIENT <chatId>] {"kind":"fetch",…,"ok":false,"error":…}` line, and on the server side the `cuisine-search-error` payload if the path is real-but-throws.
  - **Window error**: throw in DevTools console → expect `[VLOG-CLIENT <chatId>] {"kind":"window-error",…}` within ~1 s.
  - **`/log off`** → next searches should emit no VLOG lines (Railway-side); existing v0.30.4 `🔍 step …` chat trace also stops.
  - **`/log status`** (5 min after `/log on`) → expect `~ N min remaining` with N around 23 h 55 min.
  - **24-h auto-off**: verify no new VLOG lines fire after the TTL expires (operator may need to wait OR manually nuke the key via Redis CLI to spot-check earlier).

- **[KNOWN GAPS]**

  - **DF-40 — Outbound HTTP cache header logging (Places + Gemini)**: the `vlogHttp` helper exists in `verbose-log.js` but isn't wired at any call site. Wiring requires threading `chatId` (and `redis`) through `pipeline.js` + `gemini-client.js` + the Michelin Places resolver. Substantial refactor; defer to a dedicated PR. Logged in `[KNOWN GAPS]` per the standing per-PR rule.

  - **DF-41 — Unit test for the 5-s `isOn` cache + invalidate-on-enable/disable**: would need a redis-stub fixture with TTL semantics. Logged for a quiet pass.

  - **DF-42 — Per-message rate limit on `/api/vlog`**: the 4 KB payload cap is a per-call cap. A malicious / runaway TMA client could still POST hundreds of times per second. Low priority since the endpoint is gated on `isOn(chatId)` (which is owner-only-in-practice when the operator flips `/log on`), but worth adding a per-chatId 5/sec rate limit before opening verbose mode to a wider tester audience.

  - **No instrumentation on `/api/cuisine/warm-start`, `/api/cuisine/nl-query`, `/api/cuisine/place-resolve`, `/api/cuisine/place-autocomplete`, `/api/cuisine/session/*`** — those see less traffic / their failure modes are well-covered by existing logs. Easy follow-up if needed (`vlog.vlogIf` call at each entry/exit is ~6 LOC per endpoint).

  - **Doc-system updates still due**: `doc/Feature/` / `doc/Technical/` / `doc/Register/` for v0.60.158 → v0.60.161 will land in the next end-of-arc catch-up. Journal is per-PR per the standing rule.

journal.title: [HDR] #126 | 16:00:00 SGT 14-05-26 | v0.60.160 Cuisine TMA: tighten gated-category post-filter to exclude bare cuisine-name matches in review text (Portuguese precision fix) | n/a kb | 1 PR
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Operator (verbatim, with screenshots from the Cuisine TMA Portuguese search):

  > *"cuisine TMA — search criteria: Portuguese — the results are mix of different cuisine: see results below…"* — followed by a 6-card screenshot showing Smolder Seafood Grill and Bar, TINTO Spanish Restaurant, Lusitano Restaurant, Quentin's the Eurasian Restaurant, Vera Portuguese Seafood JB, Restoran Macau Express Gaya.

  Of those six: **two** are genuinely Portuguese (Lusitano, Vera Portuguese Seafood — the latter via venue name; Lusitano via `primaryType === 'portuguese_restaurant'`). The other four pass the gate because their reviews mention "Portuguese" as a cultural / flavour reference:
  - Smolder Seafood Grill — likely review mentions Portuguese-style preparations.
  - TINTO Spanish Restaurant — reviews compare to Portuguese cuisine (Iberian-peninsula proximity).
  - Quentin's the Eurasian Restaurant — Eurasian cuisine has genuine Portuguese roots (Babi Assam / Chap Chye / Kristang lineage).
  - Restoran Macau Express Gaya — review explicitly says *"baked chicken with Portuguese taste"* (Macau was a Portuguese colony for 442 years; Macanese cuisine fuses Cantonese with Portuguese).

- **[DELTA]**

  **`index.js` `/api/cuisine/search` gated-category filter (~line 9366)** — was:

  ```js
  const haystack = [
    v.name || '', v.area || '', v.primaryType || '',
    v.googleSummary?.overview || '',
    reviewText                                  // ← review text in the bare-name match
  ].join(' ').toLowerCase();
  for (const name of gatedNames) {
    const lower = name.toLowerCase();
    if (haystack.includes(lower)) return true;  // ← review mentions kept the venue
    …
    const words = lower.split(/\s+/).filter((w) => w.length >= 4);
    if (words.length >= 2 && words.every((w) => haystack.includes(w))) return true;
    const dishKeywords = require('./cuisine-dish-keywords').getDishKeywords(name);
    for (const kw of dishKeywords) {
      if (haystack.includes(kw)) return true;
    }
  }
  ```

  Now:

  ```js
  const strongHaystack = [
    v.name || '', v.area || '', v.primaryType || '',
    v.googleSummary?.overview || ''
  ].join(' ').toLowerCase();
  const fullHaystack = (strongHaystack + ' ' + reviewText).toLowerCase();
  for (const name of gatedNames) {
    const lower = name.toLowerCase();
    if (strongHaystack.includes(lower)) return true;            // bare match → STRONG only
    if (v.primaryType === `${slugForType}_restaurant`) return true;
    if (words.length >= 2 && words.every((w) => strongHaystack.includes(w))) return true;  // multi-word → STRONG only
    for (const kw of dishKeywords) {
      if (fullHaystack.includes(kw)) return true;               // dish keywords → FULL (reviews OK)
    }
  }
  ```

  **`index.js` NL chat-path gated-category filter (~line 9988)** — same change applied to the twin filter that runs on `/s` / chat-free-text searches. Keeps the two code paths in lock-step (a v0.57.12 / v0.57.13 invariant that's been honoured every time the filter has changed).

  **`package.json`** — `0.60.159 → 0.60.160` (PATCH — precision tightening, no API contract change).

  **`doc/Journal/journal-0_60_160-14_05_26-1600.md`** — this entry (#126).

   Test Files  56 passed (56)
        Tests  1740 passed (1740)        # unchanged — the filter is exercised behaviourally; the existing
                                          # cuisine-family.test.js + free-text-search.test.js cover adjacent
                                          # logic but not this specific gate. DF-39 filed for a future
                                          # mini-test that pins the strong-vs-full haystack invariant with
                                          # a fixture venue (Spanish restaurant whose reviews mention
                                          # Portuguese).
  ```

  No `web/` change in this PR → skip the cuisine TMA build per `gia-preflight`.

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy after squash-merge.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy verification matrix (Telegram, operator):

  - **Primary fix**: Open Cuisine TMA → select **Portuguese** chip → 🔍 Search. Confirm the result list now contains predominantly genuine Portuguese venues (Lusitano, Vera Portuguese Seafood JB, plus any other venues with `primaryType === 'portuguese_restaurant'` or "Portuguese" / "Portugal" in name / editorial summary). Smolder Seafood + TINTO Spanish + Restoran Macau Express should NO longer appear; Quentin's Eurasian might still appear if the editorial summary mentions Portuguese influence (acceptable — Eurasian cuisine has genuine Portuguese roots).

  - **Dish-keyword fallback still works**: a Portuguese restaurant that lacks "Portuguese" in name AND has `primaryType === 'restaurant'` (generic) but whose reviews mention `pastel de nata` / `bacalhau` / `piri piri` / etc. should still pass — those keywords are now matched against `fullHaystack` (which includes reviews). If the operator knows such a venue and it's missing from results, that's a regression.

  - **Non-regression for umbrella cuisines**: pick the umbrella **"European"** chip alone → search. Should still return a reasonable mix (Italian, Spanish, French, etc. — any venue with "European" in name/summary), since "European" appears in many such names. If the result list zeros out, the `SMALL_POOL=5` bypass kicks in (≤ 5 returned candidates skip the gate entirely).

  - **Other gated cuisines**: confirm Spanish-only, French-only, Italian-only, American-only, Mexican-only, Australian-only searches still work. The fix tightens the filter symmetrically for ALL gated-category cuisines, so each should see fewer cross-cultural false positives.

  - **Chat-path mirror**: run `/s Portuguese restaurants near me` or the equivalent NL query in chat → confirm same tightened behaviour (Smolder / TINTO / Macau Express no longer surface).

  - **`googleSummary.overview` still in STRONG haystack** — risk: if Places' editorial summary ever describes a non-Portuguese venue as "near the Portuguese settlement" or similar, that venue passes. Low-probability but theoretically possible. If it bites, demote `googleSummary.overview` to `fullHaystack` (alongside reviews) as a one-line follow-up.

  - **`SMALL_POOL = 5` bypass unchanged** — when Places returns ≤ 5 candidates, the gate is skipped entirely (preserves the operator's "European-umbrella shouldn't return zero" expectation). Could be re-evaluated if the tightened gate now leaves more pools genuinely under 5 — but the operator's report was about TOO MANY false positives, so this trade-off is acceptable.

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/App.jsx` state (line ~134)** — added `lastZeroRetrySnapRef` (a `useRef(null)` keyed by `stateSig(snap)`) and a `zeroRetried` boolean state. The ref scopes the retry-budget per-criteria signature: the same signature can never auto-retry twice, and any criteria change implicitly arms a fresh budget. The flag drives the empty-state CTA panel.

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/App.jsx::runSearch` (line ~554)** — inserted the zero-results decision block immediately after `setQuestionDeclined(false)` and before `setVenues(...)`. Four branches: (1) `isZero && !isRetryCall && lastSig !== currentSig` → set the ref, schedule `runSearch(snap, anchor, { resetSeen: true })` in `Promise.resolve().then(...)` so the current `finally { setLoading(false) }` completes first and the retry's `setLoading(true)` re-fires the spinner cleanly. (2) `isZero && isRetryCall` → the retry itself came back zero: flip `setZeroRetried(true)` + `setCriteriaOpen(true)`. (3) Non-zero result → clear both `zeroRetried` and the ref so a future zero on different criteria gets its own budget. The retry path uses `opts.resetSeen === true` as the recursion-break signal, so the chain can fire at most twice per criteria signature.

The button: re-opens the criteria builder (idempotent), clears `zeroRetried`, clears the ref, and re-fires `runSearch(state, null, { resetSeen: true })`. If the response is still zero, the silent retry guard re-arms and a fresh retry-CTA cycle plays out.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Operator (verbatim, three bullets):

  1. *"Think about how to speed up the loading of the Michelin list — doesn't start from the first in the list. investigate."*
  2. *"Bug: The Michelin review text is above the 💬 instead of the same line as 💬."*
  3. *"Result Error: 💬 '[object Object]'."*

- **[DELTA]**

  **`web/cuisine/src/v2/components/ResultCard.jsx`** (~175–179) — restructured the review line. The previous render placed `💬 "..."` in a single text node inside a plain `<div>` with no flex layout. Long review strings wrapped under the emoji, and the operator perceived 💬 as sitting on its own line. New shape uses `flex items-start gap-1` with `💬` in a dedicated `<span aria-hidden>` and the quoted text in a sibling `<span>` — emoji and text now share the first line and wrap consistently below the emoji on subsequent lines. The same edit also adds a `typeof === 'string' && .trim()` guard around the whole block so the TMA refuses to render any non-string value (defense-in-depth against issue #3).

  **`index.js`** (`handleMichelinSearch` Step 4 force-fill, ~6213–6224) — replaced the `if (!v.recentReview || !String(v.recentReview).trim())` check with `if (typeof v.recentReview !== 'string' || !v.recentReview.trim())`. The old check let a truthy non-string (e.g. `{ corrupt: 'value' }`) pass both branches because `!{ }` is false **and** `String({}).trim() === "[object Object]"` is truthy. The new check explicitly demands a string, so any non-string is immediately overwritten with the tier-aware boilerplate (`"★★★ Michelin Guide 2025 · curated recommendation."` etc.).

  **`index.js`** (`handleMichelinSearch` Step 5 cache WRITE, ~6232–6241) — sanitize every text field before writing to `michelin:enrich:<slug>`. Previously `v.recentReview || ''` would let a truthy non-string fall through; `JSON.stringify` would then serialize the object verbatim and poison the 7-day TTL'd cache for every subsequent session. Now every string field flows through `typeof v.X === 'string' ? v.X : ''` and `dishes` is array-filtered on `typeof === 'string'`. Stops the corruption at its source.

  **`index.js`** (`/api/cuisine/session/start`, ~7907–7935) — wipe every long-lived `cuisine:seen:<chatId>:*` key on TMA mount via `redis.keys()` + `redis.del()`. Previously, only the per-session clipboard (the v0.60.146 `cuisine:session-*` SET/LIST/HASH) was reset on startSession; the per-criteria seen-set (30-day TTL, keyed by criteriaHash) persisted across TMA launches, so the first 12 Michelin entries the user saw in a prior session were silently skipped on the next mount — making the catalogue appear to "start from somewhere in the middle". The operator's mental model is "fresh TMA = fresh list"; this matches it. In-session pagination still works because the seen-set advances normally during the session — it's only the long-lived persistence that's dropped.

  **`__tests__/redis-stub.js`** — added minimal `keys(pattern)` glob support (only the `*` wildcard, matching the production redis client's signature). Needed by the new session/start scan; covers all four backing stores (string / hash / set / list).

- **[INTENT]** Operator: *"The Michelin Criteria in Search Criteria of the Cuisine TMA, still load the same first 12 after tapping 'search' FAB. 1. Refresh each time the same ChatID search Michelin or Combo Search Michelin. 3. UI: Asking user to be patience, to curate the list with review."* Refined via Q&A: **(c)** force-warm Redis enrichment + **(ii)** use the existing navigation buttons (no new FAB).

- **[DELTA]**

  **(1) Bug fix — Michelin dedup: strip `radius` from the criteriaHash.**
  `handleMichelinSearch` builds its own `criteriaHash` to scope the per-criteria seen-set. The hash included `radius: searchRadius` (mirroring the cuisine-chip path) — but Michelin is a curated list, location-agnostic. Any TMA slider drift between consecutive 🔍 Search taps changed the hash → fresh seen-set → same first 12 served again. The fix omits `radius` from the Michelin criteriaHash (the cuisines + combo slugs + filters + prices + freeText + region remain). Consecutive taps now reliably reuse the same seen-set and rotate through the ~130 curated entries (`index.js:5663` block).

  **(2) Diagnostic log** at handler entry: `[Michelin] tap chatId=… hash=<8-char prefix> seen=<size> combo=[<slugs>]`. Surfaces the dedup state on every tap so the next "same first 12" report can be triaged from Railway logs in seconds (`index.js` right after `readSeenSet`). One line, never throws.

  **(3) Force-warm enrichment cache — new `michelin:enrich:<slug>` Redis key, 7-day TTL.** Distinct from the v0.60.150 `michelin:place:<slug>` Places resolution cache. After review-extract (Step 1 — existing), a new **Step 2 reads enrichment from cache** for each of the 12 venues (any missing `dishes` / `recentReview` / `vibe` / `signatureDish` is filled in from prior sessions); a **Step 3 narrate** runs only on the subset still missing `vibe` or with `dishes.length < 2` (saves Gemini cost on warmed entries; cold entries still get the LLM call); a **Step 4 force-fill** guarantees `dishes.length >= 2` and a non-empty `recentReview` on every venue (cuisine-label-based fallback dishes + a `★★★ Michelin Guide 2025 · curated recommendation.` (EN) / FR-equivalent stand-in review when no live review is available); and a **Step 5 write-back** persists the final enrichment to the cache so the NEXT search of the same chatId / criteria has the fields ready instantly. Operator's *"Check for the latest review and 2 or more dishes to try for first 12 pull and store in the server"* is exactly this: store, refresh-on-search, never ship empty.

  **(4) "Curating Michelin list" loading copy in the TMA.** New optional `loadingHint` prop on `ResultPanel` replacing the generic "Loading…" while the request is in flight. `App.jsx` sets it to *"🎩 Curating the Michelin list — fetching the latest reviews and signature dishes. Hang on…"* (EN) / *"🎩 Curation de la liste Michelin — récupération des avis récents et plats signatures. Patience…"* (FR) when `state.cuisines.includes('michelin')`, else null (falls back to the generic copy). Operator: *"UI: Asking user to be patience, to curate the list with review."*

  **Navigation** stays as-is per operator clarification — the existing 🔍 Search FAB re-fires the search and now reliably advances through the seen-set thanks to fix #1.

  $ node --check index.js

  $ npm test -- --run
   Test Files  55 passed (55)
        Tests  1728 passed (1728)
  $ cd web/cuisine && npm run build
  ✓ built  (../../public/cuisine/…)
  ```

  - Adjust the radius slider between taps → seen-set should NOT reset (this was the bug — slider drift was changing the criteriaHash → re-serving the same first 12).
  - First tap on a fresh chat → loading copy reads *"🎩 Curating the Michelin list — fetching the latest reviews and signature dishes. Hang on…"* until cards land.

Real reviews still come from `places.reviews` (when Places returns them) → the boilerplate only fires when both Places AND prior LLM narration returned nothing. Aligned with operator's "guarantee 2+ dishes + a review" without inventing review content.

For users wanting a fresh narrate per search, the cache-write step every search keeps it close — and the 7-day TTL bounds drift. A `?refreshNarrate=1` query param to force fresh narrate is a follow-up if needed.

journal.body: - **[INTENT]** Operator: *"Next build. Feature: /clipboard — 'remove' button for individual list stored. 'rename' the individual list. 'copy'."* Clarified by Q&A: **Copy = re-send as plain text** (no `/`, no map button; clean tap-hold → paste into other apps). - **[DELTA]** **`clip-store.js`** — two new helpers: - `removeClip(redis, chatId, index)` — deletes one entry by its list index using the idiomatic Redis "`LSET` sentinel + `LREM 1 sentinel`" pattern. Atomic-as-Redis-gets; returns `true` when a clip was removed. - `renameClip(redis, chatId, index, rawName)` — stamps a user-supplied `name` field onto the clip's JSON record (`LINDEX` → mutate → `LSET`). Trim + newline-collapse + 60-char cap; empty/whitespace-only names rejected. Returns the saved name or `null`. **`index.js`** — three new callback-query branches under the `clip:*` namespace: - `clip:copy:` — fetches the clip, strips `/`, unescapes `& < >`, sends without `parse_mode`. Telegram preserves the message so the user can tap-hold → Copy into other apps with clean line breaks. - `clip:rename:` — sets ephemeral `clip:rename-pending:` Redis key (5-min TTL) to the target index, sends a Telegram `force_reply` prompt *"What name for clip N? (Reply to this message — 60 chars max.)"* (EN + FR). - `clip:remove::ask` / `:yes` / `:no` — confirms inline, then `removeClip(redis, chatId, idx)`. Same confirm gate the existing `clip:clear:*` uses. **`index.js` `bot.on('message', …)`** — new pre-routing check: if `msg.reply_to_message` matches the rename prompt copy *and* a `clip:rename-pending:` value exists in Redis, apply `renameClip` to the typed text and report success (or "clip no longer exists" failure) before the rest of the message-routing pipeline. The pending key is `del`'d after a single application so a stale reply doesn't get applied later. **`index.js` `runClipCommand`** — the listing now: - **Shows the user-supplied `name` when present**, falling back to the auto-cuisines label (`escapeHtmlForTelegram`'d so an `&` in a clip name doesn't break `parse_mode: 'HTML'`). - **Renders one row per clip with 4 buttons**: `N: 📤` (Resend, existing) · `📋` (Copy as plain text, new) · `✏️` (Rename, new) · `🗑` (Remove, new). The existing 🗑 Clear all button stays on its own row at the bottom. The previous single-row "📤 1 📤 2 …" strip is replaced. **`__tests__/clip-store.test.js`** — extended the fake-Redis stub with `lSet` / `lRem`; +8 tests: - `removeClip` — removes the right entry by index, compacts; out-of-range / invalid / missing-redis no-ops. - `renameClip` — stamps `name`, leaves `body` untouched; trims + collapses newlines + caps at 60; rejects empty/whitespace; null for OOR / missing-chat. - Module-surface check: `removeClip` and `renameClip` exported. - `__tests__/redis-stub.js` — added `lIndex` / `lSet` / `lRem` matching node-redis v4 semantics (count > 0 = head-to-tail, count < 0 = tail-to-head, count === 0 = remove all). **`package.json` → `0.60.151`.** - **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]** ```bash $ node --check index.js clip-store.js (clean) $ npx vitest run __tests__/clip-store.test.js Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 25 passed (25) $ npm test -- --run Test Files 55 passed (55) Tests 1727 passed (1727) ``` - **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy after squash-merge. No frontend / TMA change — purely chat-side. - **[TEST]** Post-deploy: - `/clipboard` (or `/clip`, `/cl`) → list of up to 5 most-recent clips. Each row now has 📤 · 📋 · ✏️ · 🗑. - Tap 📋 on any clip → bot re-sends the venue block as **plain text** (no ``, no entities). Tap-hold the message → Telegram's Copy menu yields clean text. - Tap ✏️ on a clip → bot replies with a `force_reply` prompt *"What name for clip N? …"*. Type a name (e.g. "Saturday lunch Tiong Bahru"). Bot replies *"✅ Clip N renamed to 'Saturday lunch Tiong Bahru'."* The next `/clipboard` listing shows the name in the header line. - Tap 🗑 on a clip → confirm prompt (Yes, remove / Cancel). Tap Yes → that one clip is gone; the rest remain. - The existing 📤 Resend button still works (rich HTML, map button when multi-pin). - **[KNOWN GAPS]** - The plain-text Copy strips `` tags + entities; it does NOT re-format the venue block as Markdown or as a structured table. The output is the same body the user already sees, minus the HTML — readable, paste-friendly, but not "prettier". - The force-reply prompt for rename uses string-matching on the bot's own prompt text to identify the reply context (`/What name for clip|Quel nom pour le clip/i`). Future copy edits to that prompt must update the regex. (Or: switch to a sentinel field; logged but not done — low risk for two-locale strings.) - Carried-over (still owed): `doc/Feature` (partial — `feature-0_60_149-…md` landed with PR #390; needs an addendum for v0.60.150 + this PR) + `doc/Technical` + `doc/Register` + `vault/v0.60.151/` + `doc/Legal/` aggregate-usage-counts clause + `doc/VibeCodingRecord/` refresh through #390 + this PR. ---

journal.title: [HDR] #115 | 23:30:00 SGT 13-05-26 | v0.60.150 | n/a kb | 1 PR
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Operator: *"Later Michelin List — HTTP 502. Investigate."* The first Michelin tap worked (~10–15 s end-to-end after v0.60.149's slice 40→12), but the next ▶ tap returned `HTTP 502` from Railway's edge proxy. 502 = upstream timeout — Express handler didn't respond inside Railway / Telegram's webhook ceiling (~30 s).

- **[DELTA]**

  **Root cause** (diagnosed via Phase-1 Explore agent against `handleMichelinSearch` at `index.js:5713–5812`): the **12 × Places `searchText` lookups ran in a serial `for (const entry of slice) await axios.post(...)` loop**, each with a **6 s** timeout. First-tap batches returned 3★ / 2★ flagships (Odette, Burnt Ends, Les Amis, …) — popular venues with hot Google indexes, ~1–2 s per call → ~15 s total → inside the budget. Later batches dipped into the **Bib Gourmand** tier (89 stalls + obscure eateries — Places is genuinely slower on these, 3–5 s per call sometimes hitting the 6 s timeout) → 12 × 4 s = 48 s → exceeded Telegram's 30 s webhook ceiling → Railway returned 502. No response-level cache at the Michelin sub-path (the cuisine-chip `cuisine:search:*` cache is bypassed when `cuisines` includes `michelin`), so every ▶ tap re-ran the full ~48 s loop.

  **Fix — three coupled changes in `handleMichelinSearch`** (`index.js:5713–5812`, lowest-risk → highest-payoff):

  1. **Parallelize the 12 Places lookups.** Replaced the serial `for` loop with `Promise.allSettled(slice.map(async (entry) => ({ entry, placesData: await resolveEntryPlace(entry) })))`. Worst case **72 s → 4 s** in one change. (Google Places API rate is 600+ QPM per project for `searchText`; 12 parallel requests is well within budget. `pipeline.discover` uses similar concurrency for the cuisine-chip path.) The venue-object construction loop downstream is unchanged — it just iterates the resolved results instead of slicing fresh axios responses.

  2. **Per-entry Redis cache for the Places resolution.** Key `michelin:place:<slug(entry.name)>`, 24-h TTL via `setEx`. The curated Michelin entries change rarely (annual Guide refresh); Places `id` / `location` / `rating` / `reviews` / `editorialSummary` for "Odette" or "Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle" is stable for hours. Cache HIT = ~1 ms Redis read; cache MISS = the 4 s axios call. Once the catalogue is warmed (~1–3 sessions), subsequent ▶ taps for any covered entry are near-instant. Negative-cache marker `{ __null: true }` for "Places returned no match" so dead venues don't get re-hit every session.

  3. **Cut per-call axios timeout 6 s → 4 s.** Fail-fast: a Places call that takes > 4 s is almost certainly going to fail anyway; the curated entry's fallback payload (`name`, `michelinCategory`, `michelinCuisineLabel`, no `placeId`) ships either way. Aligns with the cuisine-chip `pipeline.discover` budget.

  **Diagnostic latency log.** Added a one-line `[Michelin] handler ms={n} cacheHits={h} cacheMisses={m} venues={k}` `console.warn` at the response site, fired only when `ms > 10000`. Next regression of this class will be visible in Railway logs without another investigation cycle.

  **Files**

  | File | Change |
  | :--- | :--- |
  | `index.js` `handleMichelinSearch` (lines ~5713–5812) | Replaced serial Places-resolution loop with `Promise.allSettled` over `slice.map(resolveEntryPlace)`. New inline `resolveEntryPlace(entry)` — Redis `michelin:place:<slug>` cache → axios with 4 s timeout on miss → `setEx` the result (or `{ __null: true }` on no match). Inline `slugify(s)` helper. Inline `cacheHits` / `cacheMisses` counters + `handlerStart = Date.now()` for the latency log. |
  | `index.js` (right before `return res.json({...})`) | Added the slow-handler warn log (`ms > 10000`). |
  | `__tests__/michelin-cache.test.js` (new, 9 tests) | Pins the slug helper (lowercase / non-alphanumeric → hyphen / trim / 80-cap / null-safe) and the `{ __null: true }` negative-cache marker shape. Same slug body duplicated from `index.js` so the test doesn't have to load the whole handler. |
  | `package.json` | `0.60.149 → 0.60.150`. |
  | `doc/Journal/journal-0_60_150-13_05_26-2330.md` (new) | This entry. |
  | `doc/.serial-state.yml` | `journal 114 → 115`, `commit 117 → 118`; re-anchored 13-05 '26 23:30 SGT. |

- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**

  ```bash
  $ node --check index.js
  (clean)
  $ npx vitest run __tests__/michelin-cache.test.js
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  9 passed (9)
  $ npm test -- --run
   Test Files  55 passed (55)
        Tests  1719 passed (1719)
  ```

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy after squash-merge.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy:
  - `/cuisine` → ✳️ Michelin → 🔍 → first 12 cards. Tap ▶ → next 12 → ▶ → next 12 → … keep tapping all the way through the ~130 curated entries.
  - **No 502s on any tap.** First cold tap is ~6–8 s (12 parallel Places lookups); subsequent taps with cache HITs are <2 s.
  - Railway log: at most one `[Michelin] handler ms=…` warning per cold session (the catalogue-warm pass); none on warm passes.
  - Redis: `KEYS 'michelin:place:*'` should grow to ~130 keys over a few sessions, each with a ~24-h TTL.
  - Cuisine-chip path unchanged — pick Japanese / Italian etc. → same latency and behavior as before.

- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - The LLM narrate call (`pipeline.narrateMichelinVenues`) is still a *single* batched Gemini call over 12 venues — not parallelized (already a one-shot, not 12 calls); its worst-case latency with `withRetry` `[1s, 2s, 4s]` backoff is ~25 s. Combined with the now-4 s Places fan-in, the typical cold call is ~6–8 s and the absolute worst-case is ~30 s (one Gemini retry cycle). If the Gemini latency-regresses, the `[Michelin] handler ms=…` warn log will surface it; a wall-clock guard returning partial results past 20 s remains a follow-up option.
  - The `feature-0_60_149-…md` doc is on disk (paused mid-write by this investigation) but not committed in this PR. Carried to the next doc/vault catch-up PR alongside `doc/Technical/`, `doc/Register/`, `doc/Legal/`, `vault/v0.60.150/`, and the `doc/VibeCodingRecord/` refresh through #389 + #390 (this one).

journal.title: [HDR] #114 | 21:00:00 SGT 13-05-26 | v0.60.149 | n/a kb | 1 PR
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Operator: *"Reference to PR#386, the first Michelin LLM for 40 as the loading timeout. How to solve this, reduce the list but show navigation to list 139 of them. UI: Add /clipboard to the list of /start menu, update FR. BUG: Check the code — after listing the final 80, continue back to first. Is this the best way?"*

- **[DELTA]**

  **Michelin batch 40 → 12 (the LLM-narrate timeout fix)**
  - `index.js:5689` — `sliceCap = Math.min(pool.length, 40)` → `Math.min(pool.length, 12)`. The Michelin handler now produces ≤ 12 venues per response, matching the cuisine-chip PAGE_SIZE (`web/cuisine/src/v2/components/ResultPanel.jsx:30`). The LLM narrate prompt at `pipeline.js narrateMichelinVenues` operates on 12 venues — comfortably inside Gemini's retry budget + Telegram's ~30 s webhook ceiling. Per-tap latency drops to ~3-5 s.
  - The existing per-criteria seen-set (`cuisine:seen:<chatId>:<criteriaHash>`) rotates the pool across consecutive ▶ taps; after ~11 taps the user has walked all ~130 curated Michelin entries (operator's "list 139 of them"), then `didReset = true` recycles the per-criteria set (existing v0.60.42+ behavior).
  - Updated the surrounding comment block at `index.js:5680-5693` recording the history (v0.60.42 set it to 40 to cap Places-API latency; v0.60.147 added the LLM narrate step on top, which pushed past Telegram's window; v0.60.149 drops to 12 to bring it back).

  **Michelin × 80-cap interaction**
  - The Michelin curated list (~130 entries) needs to be walkable in one session. The cuisine-wide 80-cap session SET (`cuisine:session-seen:<chatId>`) would have terminated it at 80 — so Michelin now opts out of the cap.
  - `cuisine-session.js` `recordPage(redis, chatId, payload, opts)` — new `opts.skipCap` parameter. When `skipCap === true`, the helper:
    - does NOT `SADD` the venue placeIds into the session-seen SET (so they don't count toward the 80),
    - still LPUSHes the page payload onto the page-history LIST (so the ⇠ Prev FAB walks Michelin pages too),
    - always returns `capped: false` regardless of how many venues have been served this session.
  - `handleMichelinSearch` (`index.js:6038-6055`) — passes `{ skipCap: true }` to `recordPage`. The local `michelinSessionFull` variable is removed; the response now always reports `sessionFull: false` for Michelin (its own exhaustion is the `didReset` path on the per-criteria seen-set, unchanged).

  **`/clipboard` added to the BotFather setMyCommands menu (EN + FR)**
  - `index.js` `enCommands` array (line 6828, after `/search`):
    `{ command: 'clipboard', description: '📋 Saved cuisine clips · latest from /cuisine Copy-all / per-card Copy (or /clip)' }`
  - `frCommands` array (matching insertion point):
    `{ command: 'clipboard', description: '📋 Clips de cuisine enregistrés · les plus récents depuis /cuisine (ou /clip)' }`
  - `/clip` and `/cl` remain regex-only aliases (not in the menu — they're shortcuts). `/clipboard` becomes the canonical menu surface. The chat-handler regex at `index.js:1831` already matches all three (added in v0.60.148, PR #387).

  **Post-80 ↻ Recycle button**
  - **New endpoint** `POST /api/cuisine/session/recycle` in `index.js` — `verifyInitData`, then `cuisineSession.startSession(redis, chatId)` (wipes session-seen + session-pages + session-meta), then `usageLog.recordSearch(redis, chatId, { src: 'cuisine-tma-recycle' })` so Oversight tracks the recycle as its own event. Returns `{ ok: true }`. Never blocks the TMA — falls back to `{ ok: false }` on any error.
  - **New API helper** `recycleSession()` in `web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/api.js`, mirrors `startSession()` / `backOnePage()`.
  - **`App.jsx` terminal-note block** — when `sessionFull === true`, the existing `↺ Start over` button (which only wipes the per-criteria seen-set, not the 80-cap session SET) is replaced by a **↻ Recycle** button. Handler: `await recycleSession(); setVenues([]); setSessionFull(false); setExhaustedNote(false); setPageStackDepth(0); runSearch(state)` — wipes local + server state and re-fires the same search, returning list #1 again. Terminal copy updated EN + FR.
    - EN: *"You've seen the 80 maximum for this session. Tap ↻ Recycle to start a fresh session (list #1 again), or close and re-open Cuisine."*
    - FR: *"Vous avez vu le maximum de 80 lieux pour cette session. Touchez ↻ Recycler pour redémarrer (liste n°1 à nouveau), ou fermez et ré-ouvrez Cuisine."*
  - **Why explicit button instead of silent auto-loop** — auto-loop would silently reset the session and serve the same first 12 venues without warning, which is a UX surprise (the operator might think pagination broke). The explicit ↻ button is one tap, no surprise, and the action is clear.

  **Tests** — `__tests__/cuisine-session.test.js` gains a 4-test `describe('recordPage opts.skipCap')` block: capped=false past 80, session-seen never grows, page-history still records (back-FAB still works on Michelin), cuisine-chip + Michelin can interleave in the same session without contaminating each other's seen-set.

  **`package.json` → `0.60.149`.**

- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**

  ```bash
  $ node --check index.js cuisine-session.js
  (clean)
  $ npm test -- --run
   Test Files  54 passed (54)
        Tests  1710 passed (1710)
  $ cd web/cuisine && npm run build
  ✓ built  (../../public/cuisine/…)
  ```

- **[STATUS]** STAGED → PROD on next Railway deploy. The GitHub MCP server disconnected during this session, so the PR is opened via the GitHub web UI rather than `mcp__github__create_pull_request`.

- **[TEST]** Post-deploy:
  - `/cuisine` → ✳️ Michelin → 🔍 → 12 cards with vibe + dishes + recentReview returned within ~5 s (was: timed out at 40). Tap ▶ → next 12, then ▶ again, … keep going for ~11 taps to walk all ~130 curated entries. The 80-cap **does not** stop the walk on Michelin.
  - Open Telegram `/` autocomplete → `/clipboard` is now in the menu with its EN description; in the FR Telegram client the FR text shows. Tapping it lists the user's last 50 cuisine clips (same handler as `/clip`).
  - `/cuisine` → pick Japanese + Korean → tap ▶ until the 80-cap terminal. Terminal copy now ends with **↻ Recycle**. Tap → server wipes session-seen + session-pages + session-meta, re-fires `runSearch`, list #1 returns. `usage:criteria` in Oversight shows `src:cuisine-tma-recycle` incrementing.

- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - **Silent auto-loop variant.** Operator proposed *"continue back to first"* which I read as auto-loop. Shipped the explicit-button version (less surprising). If operator wants pure silent auto-loop on the next ▶, it's a one-line change at the top of `runSearch` (`if (sessionFull) await recycleSession();`) — flagged for a follow-up if requested.
  - **Michelin × ⇠ Prev across paths.** Page history is session-scoped and shared across cuisine-chip / Michelin / freetext (always was). Walking 11 Michelin ▶ taps now fills the page-history LIST (cap 10 → only the last 10 Michelin pages are walkable backward). Going further back than 10 pages is not supported by design; the existing TTL + cap balance favours the back-FAB feeling responsive over preserving every page.
  - Still owed (carried across the arc): `doc/Feature/` + `doc/Technical/` + `doc/Register/` catch-up for v0.60.142 → v0.60.149; `vault/v0.60.149/` snapshot; `doc/Legal/` aggregate-usage-counts clause; `doc/VibeCodingRecord/` refresh to include #384, #385, #386, #387 and the v0.60.149 PR.
