journal.title: [HDR] #60 | 15:30:00 SGT 01-05-26 | v0.30.2 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Four simultaneous Human Lead reports bundled into one PR:
  1. **`/ver` red on Gemini** — `gemini-2.5-pro:generateContent [503 Service Unavailable]`. User had `GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-pro` set in Railway env; Pro overloaded; bot bricks even though Flash is fine.
  2. **`/surprise` returns "Meaningless outcome"** — strict gates (4-day fresh-review window) too aggressive for SG's review velocity on small venues.
  3. **TMA doesn't show what location it's using** — user wants resolved coords visible in the Header.
  4. **NL classifier mishandles "My location change"** — typed phrase got gatekept as off-topic; classifier needs `update-location` intent.
  5. **15-min staleness reminder missing** — picks just keep using cached location forever silently.
- **[DELTA — Gemini Pro→Flash auto-fallback]**
  - **`gemini-retry.js`** — `withRetry` accepts a new `fallbackFn` option. After exhausting retries on a 429/503, if `fallbackFn` is provided AND the error was retryable (transient), invokes it once. Bubbles non-retryable errors immediately (auth/bad-request/schema — Flash won't fix those).
    + new `makeFlashFallback(genAI, prompt, generationConfig)` helper. Returns `null` when `GEMINI_MODEL` is already `gemini-2.5-flash` (no fallback target makes sense). Otherwise returns a function that calls Flash with the same prompt + generationConfig.
    + `FLASH_MODEL` constant exported.
  - All six Gemini call sites updated to pass `fallbackFn: makeFlashFallback(...)`:
    - `nl-intent.js#classifyIntent`
    - `pipeline.js#reason` (D610)
    - `pipeline.js#refine` (D630)
    - `surprise.js#geminiEnrich`
    - `cuisine-search.js#geminiCandidates15`
    - `vibe-suggest.js#geminiCandidates`
  - When fallback fires, log line: `[<label>] primary model exhausted N retries on transient error; falling back to flash: <err>`. Permanent fallback log: `[<label>] fallback also failed: <err>`.
- **[DELTA — /surprise gate relaxation]**
  - **`surprise.js`** — `RECENT_REVIEW_DAYS` raised from `4` → `30`. Original 4-day gate was below SG's typical review-velocity for hidden-gem (<50-review) venues, so every search returned empty. The original 4-day signal preserved as `STRICT_RECENT_DAYS` constant (unused as a gate, available as a soft-preference signal in future patches).
  - **`findSurprise`** restructured from "return-on-first-pass" to "remember-soft-fallback-then-finalize" — first opening-gate-passing venue is held as `softFallback`. If a later venue passes the (now 30-day) recent-review gate, it overrides. If no venue ever passes, the soft fallback is returned with `isFallback: true` flag.
  - **`index.js#deliverSurprise`** — when `v.isFallback === true`, appends a transparent footer: `💡 Best match in your annulus — no fresh review this week, but rating + price profile fits.` User gets a real venue instead of "no gem".
- **[DELTA — location-update intent + staleness reminder]**
  - **`location-cache.js`** — `setUserLocation` now stamps `setAt: Date.now()` on the stored payload. Backwards-compat for pre-v0.30.2 entries (treats `null` `setAt` as unknown age). New helper `getLocationAgeMinutes(redis, chatId)` returns minutes since the user last shared/typed a location.
  - **`nl-intent.js`** — added new intent `"update-location"`. Prompt examples cover English ("My location change", "I moved to Bishan") + Mandarin ("我换地方了"). Whitelist updated.
  - **`index.js#bot.on('message')`** — new `update-location` branch BEFORE the food/drinks/groceries dispatch. On match, drops any pending state and surfaces `LOCATION_REQUEST_KEYBOARD` with the localised ack text. Diagnostic code **D754** logged.
  - **`index.js#deliverPicks`** — after delivery, if `getLocationAgeMinutes(...) >= 15`, fires a fire-and-forget reminder: `📍 Heads up — your location is N min old. Type "my location changed" or share a new pin to refresh.` So users don't drift on stale coords without realising.
  - **`web/cuisine/src/components/Header.jsx`** — adds a third line under the title showing current resolved location: `📍 1.3030, 103.8364` (or `📍 (location not set)` when null). Re-detect button stays in place. User now always knows what coords Gia is using.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on surprise.js, index.js, gemini-retry.js, pipeline.js,
                cuisine-search.js, nl-intent.js, vibe-suggest.js → OK
  ```
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[OPERATIONAL — Human Lead's immediate fix path for /ver red]**
  Two options:
  1. **Switch model env**: Railway → `GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash` (or just delete the var; default is Flash). Save → auto-redeploy → /ver green within ~30 s.
  2. **Keep Pro, rely on auto-fallback**: leave `GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-pro`; v0.30.2 will retry-then-Flash on every 503. Slightly more latency on Pro outages but no env change needed.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - Auto-fallback adds ~7 s of retry+wait before Flash actually runs. During an outage, every Gemini call pays this. Tunable by shortening `delays` in `gemini-retry.js`.
  - The fallback to Flash uses the SAME prompt that was tuned for Pro. Since Pro and Flash have similar JSON-mode behaviour, this works in practice. If output quality regresses noticeably, consider per-model prompt variants.
  - `/ver` still calls the configured model directly (no fallback wrapper) — by design, so the health probe reports the actual configured-model state, not a softened-via-fallback state.
  - Soft-fallback for `/surprise` may surface venues with stale-ish reviews (>4 days, ≤30 days). Banner discloses the trade.

journal.title: [HDR] #59 | 15:15:00 SGT 01-05-26 | v0.30.1 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead "Test that Gemini API and google Map aPI is working but firing this: Find newly opened Peranakan, Indonesian, Middle Eastern, or Korean restaurants…". User wants to verify the v0.30.0 NL pipeline end-to-end with a complex query without typing into chat. Extend `/admin/test-pipeline` to accept `nl_text` so a single curl runs `classifyIntent` → merge hints → full `searchCuisine` pipeline → returns trace.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`index.js#GET /admin/test-pipeline`** — three new query params:
    - `nl_text` — free-text query (any language). When present, runs `classifyIntent` first; merges extracted `cuisines` + `special_request` into the pipeline call. Explicit `cuisines=`/`specialRequest=` query params take precedence.
    - `specialRequest` (alias `special_request`) — bypass the classifier and inject the qualifier directly.
    - `lang` — language hint passed to `classifyIntent` (default `en`).
    - + new `trace.steps.nl` block returns `{intent, confidence, cuisines, special_request, lang, ack_text}` so user sees the classifier's full output in the JSON response.
  - **`searchCuisine` invocation** in this route now also threads `specialRequest` so the test endpoint exercises the same Gemini reason prompt path as the chat NL flow.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on index.js → OK
  ```
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[OPERATIONAL TEST FOR HUMAN LEAD'S TEST QUERY]**
  After Railway redeploys, run:
  ```
  curl -G "https://<webhookDomain>/admin/test-pipeline" \\
    --data-urlencode "secret=<ADMIN_SYNC_SECRET>" \\
    --data-urlencode "nl_text=Find newly opened Peranakan, Indonesian, Middle Eastern, or Korean restaurants within 1 km of Singapore CBD MRT stations like Tanjong Pagar and Raffles Place that have launched in the last six months, and provide a list including their specific opening dates, signature dishes, and direct Google Maps URLs for easy navigation while excluding major fast-food chains." \\
    --data-urlencode "lat=1.2839" \\
    --data-urlencode "lng=103.8517" \\
    --data-urlencode "radius=1000" \\
    --data-urlencode "recencyDays=180"
  ```
  Expected response shape:
  ```json
  {
    "version": "0.30.1",
    "env": { "PIPELINE_ENABLED": true, "GEMINI_API_KEY_present": true, "GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY_present": true, "REDIS_open": true },
    "params": {...},
    "steps": {
      "nl": {
        "intent": "food",
        "confidence": 0.95,
        "cuisines": ["Peranakan","Indonesian","Korean"],   // Middle Eastern parses to Lebanese/Persian/etc — classifier picks closest
        "special_request": "newly opened in last 6 months, no fast-food chains",
        "lang": "en",
        "ack_text": "🌿 Searching for newly opened Peranakan / Indonesian / Korean / Middle Eastern restaurants…"
      },
      "vault": { "n_vault": 0|N, ... },
      "pipeline": {
        "venuesCount": 5,
        "firstFewVenues": [{ "name", "placeId", "queueMinEstimate", "costEstimateSgd", "travelAdvice", "shelterNote", "signatureDish" }],
        ...
      }
    },
    "totalMs": 9000
  }
  ```
- **[DECISION TREE FOR INTERPRETING THE RESPONSE]**
  - `env.GEMINI_API_KEY_present === false` → key not configured. Set in Railway.
  - `env.GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY_present === false` → key not configured.
  - `steps.nl.error` → classifier failed to call Gemini (network / auth). Gemini is broken or quota exhausted.
  - `steps.nl.intent === 'other'` or `confidence < 0.6` → classifier didn't classify as food (unexpected for this query — would indicate Gemini Flash interpreting it strangely).
  - `steps.vault.n_vault === 0` → vault index empty. Run `/admin/sync-vault` first (Open #17).
  - `steps.pipeline.venuesCount === 0` → reason returned candidates but Places-validate filtered all (likely the GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY 403 from Open #4, even after the user marked it done — re-verify referrer settings).
  - `steps.pipeline.venuesCount > 0` → **both APIs are firing correctly**, NL pipeline works end-to-end. Confirms Gemini + Maps + Refine pipeline.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - Single curl runs the full pipeline including 2 Gemini calls (classify + reason + refine = 3 total) + ≤15 Places validates. Cost ~$0.07–$0.10 per test. Don't loop.
  - `nl_text` request bodies can be long; the URL-encoded form may bump up against URL length limits on some proxies. If hit, switch to POST + JSON body. Acceptable for now.
  - No throttling; auth-gated by `ADMIN_SYNC_SECRET`. Don't share that secret publicly.

journal.title: [HDR] #58 | 15:00:00 SGT 01-05-26 | v0.30.0 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead "Can I type anything in the bot chat and you search as well? But you can referee if I am not search anything related to cuisine, groceries, food or drinks and it can be multiple languages… Example, show me Michelin star food in Mandarin or Arabic or French". Open up free-text chat as a first-class entry point with multi-language support and intent gating.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **NEW** `nl-intent.js` — `classifyIntent({text, langCode, redis})` calls Gemini Flash with a structured prompt that:
    1. Classifies intent: `food` | `drinks` | `groceries` | `other`
    2. Extracts canonical English cuisines from our 73-entry catalogue (matches `web/cuisine/src/state/cuisines.js`)
    3. Extracts `special_request` (free-form qualifier — "Michelin-starred", "halal", "vegetarian", "kid-friendly", "late-night", "outdoor seating", "budget under $20", etc.)
    4. Detects input language (ISO 639-1)
    5. Generates `ack_text` in the SAME language as input
    Cached per `(langCode, sha1(text))` for 60 s in Redis. Confidence threshold = 0.6 — below that we fall through to the existing gatekeeper.
  - **`index.js`** — new free-text branch in `bot.on('message')` between the pending-meal consume and the gatekeeper:
    1. Skip slash commands + keyboard taps (existing guards).
    2. Call `classifyIntent` (~1.5–2 s).
    3. If intent ∈ {food, drinks, groceries} and confidence ≥ 0.6:
       - Send `ack_text` (in user's language) to chat.
       - If location cached: dispatch `runNLFlow(chatId, lat, lng, {cuisines, specialRequest, intent})`.
       - If no location: stash payload as `nl:<json>` pending state, prompt `LOCATION_REQUEST_KEYBOARD`. Resumes once location arrives.
    4. Else: fall through to existing `gatekeep(redis, text)` (off-topic steering).
  - + `runNLFlow(chatId, lat, lng, payload)` — calls `searchCuisine` with `cuisines` + `specialRequest` + sensible defaults (radius 1km, recency 90d, queue 15min, walk, now). Delivers via `deliverPicks`.
  - + Pending-state extension — `resolvePending` recognises `nl:<json-payload>` prefix, returns `{kind: 'nl', cuisines, specialRequest, intent, lang}`. All three location-resume sites (default-Raffles fallback, location-share keyboard, place-name typed) now branch on `resolved.kind === 'nl'` to call `runNLFlow`.
  - + Diagnostic codes (Railway-side only — `[NL-Intent]` prefix):
    - **D750** received chat=N lang=… bytes=N
    - **D751** dispatching intent=food confidence=0.9
    - **D752** runNLFlow failed (catch path)
    - **D753** falls through (intent=other or low confidence)
  - **`cuisine-search.js`** — `searchCuisine` accepts `specialRequest` (default empty); `buildPrompt` and `geminiCandidates15` and pipeline `runPipeline.query` all thread it through. New prompt line: `Distinctive user qualifier (HONOUR THIS): <special_request>` so Gemini surfaces venues matching the qualifier.
  - **`pipeline.js`** — `buildReasonPrompt` adds the same line when `query.specialRequest` is present.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on index.js, nl-intent.js, cuisine-search.js, pipeline.js → OK
  node -e "require('./nl-intent')" → exports {classifyIntent, MIN_CONFIDENCE, CUISINE_CATALOGUE: 73 entries}
  ```
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. After deploy: type "Show me Michelin star food" → Bot acks "🌿 Searching for Michelin-starred restaurants near you…", then if location cached, returns 5 picks with refined cost / queue / dishes per usual; if no location, prompts to share.
  2. Type "推荐附近的米其林法餐" → ack in 中文: "🌿 正在为您搜寻附近的米其林法式餐厅…". Picks delivered same as above with `cuisines: ["French"]` + `special_request: "Michelin-starred"`.
  3. Type "اعرض لي مطاعم حاصلة على نجمة ميشلان" → ack in Arabic.
  4. Type "tell me about quantum physics" → falls through to existing gatekeeper. No Gemini food call.
  5. Type "thanks!" → low-confidence other; gatekeeper steers.
  6. Railway logs: every classification logs `[NL-Intent] D750 → D751 dispatching intent=food confidence=0.95 cuisines=French special="Michelin-starred" lang=zh`.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - Sanctuary read text (after picks) stays English. Only the ack message is multilingual. Localising the entire deliverPicks output would require a second Gemini round per delivery; deferred until v0.31.x or via translate-on-tap.
  - `MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.6` — tunable via env var if false-positives surface ("How was your day?" might trip on "day" near "food" mention). Currently hardcoded.
  - Cache key folds language code so the same text in different `language_code` headers is treated as distinct cache entries (correct — same text could have different intent across languages).
  - Voice input deferred to v0.30.1 (next PR).

journal.title: [HDR] #57 | 14:45:00 SGT 01-05-26 | v0.29.3 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead diagnostic screenshot — the v0.29.2 Diagnostics panel finally exposed the failure mode: D406 fired at 6 s into a request that legitimately needs 8–15 s end-to-end. The 6 s `searchCuisine` fetch timeout was below pipeline p50 latency, so EVERY happy-path search was tripping the dual-channel fallback, which in turn auto-closed the TMA per Telegram's sendData spec. The user's complaint "/cuisine screen closes so fast" is the visible symptom of this self-inflicted abort.
- **[ROOT CAUSE TRACE FROM SCREENSHOT]**
  ```
  ✓ D100 TMA mounted
  ✓ D060 Launch context · iOS 9.6, initData 579 chars
  ✓ D050 GET /api/diag/cuisine
  ✓ D200 Requesting browser geolocation
  ✓ D300 initData present · len=579
  ✓ D201 Got location · 1.3030, 103.8364
  ✓ D051 Bridge OK · pipelineOn=true, elapsedMs=209
  ✓ D400 onSearch invoked
  ✓ D401 Payload built · n_cuisines=0, radius=1000
  ✓ D402 POST /api/cuisine-search (6s timeout)
  ✗ D406 Fetch timed out (>6s)        ← here
  ✗ D404 HTTP 0 · null
  ✗ D063 Primary fetch failed, trying sendData fallback
  ✓ D061 sendData fallback dispatched  → TMA closes by Telegram spec
  ```
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`web/cuisine/src/api/search.js`** — `searchCuisine` default `timeoutMs` raised from `6000` → `25000`. Documented inline why: pipeline is 9–11 s typical (Reason ~3 s + Validate ~3–4 s + Refine ~2–3 s); the previous 6 s was below p50 and triggered fallback unnecessarily.
  - **`web/cuisine/src/App.jsx`** — banner copy updated from "Sensing the vibe… (this may take 5–10 s)" to "Sensing the vibe… (8–15 s typical — Reason → Fetch → Refine)" so the user mental-models the actual duration. D402 log label updated to `(25s timeout)`.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  cd web/cuisine && npm run build → vite v5.4.21 ✓ in 2.84s
    → public/cuisine/assets/index-*.js  172.72 kB (gzip 56.80 kB)
  ```
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. Force-refresh TMA. Header reads `v0.29.3`.
  2. Tap Search → banner reads "Sensing the vibe… (8–15 s typical — Reason → Fetch → Refine)".
  3. Wait. Cards should render in-place 8–15 s later (no TMA close).
  4. Toggle 🔧 Debug → Diagnostics shows `D402 POST /api/cuisine-search (25s timeout)` then `D403 HTTP 200` then `D502 Received N venues` — no D406, no D063, no fallback. TMA stays open.
  5. The sendData fallback path is preserved for genuine network/server failures (network drop, 500 from server, >25 s pipeline hang). It just no longer fires on the happy path.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - 25 s is generous; if Gemini hangs hard the user waits the full 25 s before fallback. Acceptable trade vs. mid-search abort. Express has no default request timeout; could add a server-side `req.setTimeout(20000)` to bound long-tail. Deferred.
  - We're documenting that the pipeline is intrinsically multi-second by design (Reason → Fetch → Refine). To shorten meaningfully would mean dropping a phase, which is a product decision.
  - The v0.29.2 visible 🔧 Debug button + Diagnostics-under-Header is what made this diagnosable. Keep it as a permanent fixture even after the underlying bugs resolve.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Two diagnostic surfaces in response to Human Lead "/ver shows everything green but no prompt syntax sending to Gemini" + "How to press D":
  1. `/admin/test-pipeline` — black-box endpoint that bypasses TMA + initData and runs the SAME pipeline server-side, returning a step-by-step trace. Definitively answers "is the bridge broken or is the pipeline broken?"

Picked: enrich the Refine-pipeline per-cluster context with **nearest MRT stations** so travel advice can anchor on a real station ("3 min walk from Raffles Place MRT") rather than the generic "transit clear" copy. `transport.nearestMrtStations` already existed (since the v0.20.0-era `/transport` work) — it just wasn't wired into the cuisine pipeline.

Same `Promise.allSettled` failure tolerance — MRT lookup failure does not block the pipeline.
- **[DELTA — cache-bust + bundle visibility]** Added in response to mid-PR Human Lead "Test why still cannot search… is telegram block ai syntax":
  - **`index.js`** — new `noCacheHtml(res)` helper sets `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0` + `Pragma: no-cache` + `Expires: 0` on every TMA HTML response (`/app`, `/app/menu`, `/app/cuisine`, `/app/map`). Vite-built assets remain cacheable (content-hashed filenames). This closes the "Railway redeployed but Telegram still serves the stale bundle" failure mode.

User can confirm at-a-glance which bundle they're running without opening console or Diagnostics.     1. Force-refresh: close the TMA, swipe-up to kill Telegram, reopen, tap the chat menu button.
    2. Verify the Header now reads `v0.29.0`.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead "Can you do 2" — outstanding-list item #2 (`Run node sync-vault.js once to populate the curated 14-venue Vault`). I cannot run the script from sandbox (no production GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, no production REDIS_URL, no Railway CLI). Instead, ship an auth-gated HTTPS endpoint that runs the import in-process on Railway using the bot's existing connections.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`sync-vault.js`** — refactored to expose a callable. The main() CLI entrypoint preserved; module now also exports:
    - `runSync({redis, items?, fenceDisabled?})` — accepts a *connected* Redis client (so we don't open a second connection alongside the bot's). Returns `{imported, skippedClosed, fenced, failed, vaultCount, samples, durationMs, fenceDisabled, inputCount}`. `samples` carries the first 5 imported display-names so the route response previews what landed without dumping the full list.
    - `resolveInputs()` — file-system input resolver (data/Saved Places.json, data/My Maps/*.kmz, fallback to HARDCODED_URLS).
    - `HARDCODED_URLS` — the 14-URL fallback list.
    - CLI-vs-required guard at EOF (`if (require.main === module)`) so requiring the module from the route doesn't auto-run main().
    - Behaviour preserved: `requireEnv('GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY')` runs in main() but `runSync` validates it inline so a missing env throws cleanly to the route's catch.
  - **`index.js`** —
    - + `GET /admin/sync-vault?secret=<ADMIN_SYNC_SECRET>` — auth-gated, server-side import.
    - Auth: timing-safe compare (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`) on the secret query param against `process.env.ADMIN_SYNC_SECRET`. Missing env → 503 with hint to set it. Wrong secret → 401.
    - On success: invokes `runSync({redis, fenceDisabled: req.query.fence === 'off'})`, then `vaultIndex.refreshIndex(redis)` so the in-memory snapshot picks up the new venues immediately (no 5-min cron wait). Returns `{ok: true, ...summary}` JSON.
    - Logs `[Admin] /admin/sync-vault triggered by IP=<ip>` on entry, `[Admin] sync-vault complete: <json>` on success, `[Admin] sync-vault failed: <msg>` on error.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on index.js, sync-vault.js → OK
  node -e "require('./sync-vault')"  → exports {runSync, resolveInputs, HARDCODED_URLS}, 14 URLs ✓
  ```
  Live import requires production Redis + Maps key; verified post-deploy by the Human Lead.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[OPERATIONAL RUNBOOK]**
  1. Generate a long random string for `ADMIN_SYNC_SECRET`. Suggested: `openssl rand -base64 32`.
  2. Railway → Service → Variables → add `ADMIN_SYNC_SECRET=<that string>`. Redeploy.
  3. Once Railway has redeployed, run:
     ```
     curl "https://<webhookDomain>/admin/sync-vault?secret=<that string>"
     ```
     Response is JSON: `{ok: true, imported: N, skippedClosed: M, fenced: K, failed: J, vaultCount: V, samples: [...], durationMs: <ms>, fenceDisabled: false, inputCount: 14}`.
  4. Tail Railway logs concurrently to see per-venue `[Sync]  <name> (<placeId>)` lines.
  5. Verify with `/cuisine` Search — Diagnostics panel should show `D601 Vault snapshot` with `n_vault > 0`.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - Endpoint is rate-limit-free and synchronous — a long import (e.g. 200 venues with the future Tranche-B dataset) ties up an Express worker for ~1 min. For the current 14-URL fallback this is fine (~10 s end-to-end). If we ever expand, refactor to background-job pattern.
  - Endpoint accepts `?fence=off` to disable the Singapore-fence (mirrors the CLI `--no-fence` flag). Honest documentation: the fence is a safety net to drop accidental out-of-SG entries; don't disable unless you know you're importing non-SG venues deliberately.
  - The sync-vault main() CLI path is unchanged — `node sync-vault.js` still works for local testing.
  - `vault-index.refreshIndex(redis)` runs after sync so `pipeline.reason()` sees new venues immediately. The 5-min cron continues to refresh from any other writes.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Outstanding-list item #3: 60-second per-chat pick cache. v0.26.0 noted ~$0.07/search end-to-end (Reason + Validate + Refine = 2 Gemini + ≤15 Place Details + 1 Routes Matrix). Tap-spam (user taps Search, sees results, taps again to confirm, mucks with sliders, taps a third time) currently bills 3× full pipeline. The cache deduplicates near-identical requests within a 60 s window for ~80% cost cut on the spam pattern.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **NEW** `pick-cache.js` — Redis-backed cache with `get/set/keyFor/TTL_S`. Cache key folds:
    - `chatId` (per-user, prevents cross-tenant leakage)
    - `lat/lng` snapped to a 100 m grid (0.0009° lat-deg) — typo-tolerant within a city block
    - `radius`, `recencyDays`, `queueMaxMin`, `mode`, `when`, `preset`
    - `cuisines` lower-cased + sorted + pipe-joined
    Smoke-tested: two requests with `(1.2839, 103.8517)` vs `(1.28391, 103.85171)` and `[Japanese, Korean]` vs `[Korean, Japanese]` collapse to the same key.
  - **`index.js#POST /api/cuisine-search`** — cache lookup before pipeline dispatch; cache write-through after a successful response with non-empty venues. Diag codes:
    - **D705** cache HIT (returns cached payload + `{cached: true}` flag, ~50 ms instead of ~9 s)
    - **D706** cache STORE (TTL = 60 s)

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead "I still cannot fire the prompt in TMA". v0.26.3's dual-channel bridge addressed *post-tap* failure modes (HTTP 4xx/5xx, network throw, sendData fallback). It did NOT address three *pre-tap* / *no-feedback* modes that look identical to the user as "nothing happens":
  1. **Geolocation never resolves** → `state.loc` stays null → `onSearch` returns early after `showAlert('Tap 📍 first.')` which may be invisible in some Telegram clients.
  2. **The "Sensing the vibe…" banner** only paints when `state.loading` flips, which requires the early-return check to pass first.
  3. **No fetch timeout** — if HTTPS hangs (slow Gemini, blocked webview, hostile MDM), neither HTTP error nor sendData fallback fires.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`web/cuisine/src/api/search.js#searchCuisine`** — added `AbortController` with default 6 s timeout. On timeout returns `{status: 0, ok: false, body: null, timedOut: true}` so the App-level fallback path treats it identically to a network failure.
  - **`web/cuisine/src/App.jsx`** —
    - + `CBD_DEFAULT = {lat: 1.2839, lng: 103.8517}` constant. When `state.loc` is null at Search time, we use CBD-centre as a hard default instead of blocking the search. Recorded as `D202 Geolocation unavailable — proceeding with CBD default`.
    - + `searchTaps` counter rendered on the Search button label as `🔍 Search · N` after the first tap. Manifestly visible proof the click handler fired.
    - + `bannerText` state. `setBannerText('🌿 Sensing the vibe… (this may take 5–10 s)')` is the FIRST line of `onSearch` so the user sees feedback BEFORE any state update or async work. Cleared on `searchOk`.
    - + `forceChatDelivery()` — a separate handler that bypasses fetch entirely and pushes the payload via `Telegram.WebApp.sendData()` immediately. Useful for hostile-webview environments. Surfaced as a small `💬 Chat` button next to Search.
    - + `buildPayload()` factored out so both `onSearch` and `forceChatDelivery` use the same payload shape.
    - + Inline geolocation hint copy changed from "Tap 📍 above to share your location." to "📍 unavailable — Search will use CBD default. Tap 📍 above to share your real location." so the user understands the search will *still work* without it.
    - + Timeout branch in `onSearch`: `result.timedOut` records `D406 Fetch timed out (>6s)` and triggers the existing dual-channel fallback (sendData → web_app_data → chat delivery).
  - **`web/cuisine/src/main.jsx`** — `console.log('[Cuisine-Diag] D040 bundle loaded version=0.26.4')` on bundle load. New diag code D040 confirms the freshly-built JS is what the browser is actually executing (vs. a stale cached asset) — closes a "we shipped it but is the user running it?" debugging hole.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  cd web/cuisine && npm run build → vite v5.4.21 ✓ in 1.26s
    → public/cuisine/assets/index-*.js  167.57 kB (gzip 54.32 kB)
  ```
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. Open `/cuisine` → browser console immediately shows `[Cuisine-Diag] D040 bundle loaded version=0.26.4`. Confirms a fresh bundle.
  2. Block location in Settings (don't tap Allow). Tap **🔍 Search** anyway → button label updates to `🔍 Search · 1`, banner appears "🌿 Sensing the vibe…" within ~50 ms, search proceeds with CBD default. Diagnostics records `D202 Geolocation unavailable — proceeding with CBD default`. Picks return based on Raffles Place.
  3. Allow location, tap Search. If HTTPS reaches the server, picks render in the TMA. If the server hangs >6 s, console shows `D406 Fetch timed out (>6s)` → `D063 → D061`, TMA closes, picks arrive in chat.
  4. Tap **💬 Chat** instead — TMA closes within 800 ms, picks arrive in chat. Bypasses fetch entirely.
  5. Tap Search rapidly 5 times in 2 seconds → counter shows `🔍 Search · 5`. Even if all fail, the user has unambiguous proof their taps were received.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - The 6 s timeout is generous for Reason+Refine pipeline (~5–11 s typical) but tight for slow networks. May abort legitimate slow searches; the sendData fallback catches those, so the user still gets results, just delivered to chat instead of in-TMA.
  - CBD default is hard-coded to Raffles Place. Singapore-only product; acceptable. If we ever expand outside SG, replace with a country-default lookup.

journal.title: [HDR] #45 | 11:30:00 SGT 01-05-26 | v0.26.3 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead 4-part repair spec restating the bridge failure ("Search button currently fails to deliver the user's prompt to the server, resulting in no response"). The escalation past v0.26.1's pre-flight ping + chat receipt names a real Telegram WebApp gap I underestimated:

  > "verify the launch context of the TMA; if the app is launched via a KeyboardButton, configure the Search button to use Telegram.WebApp.sendData() to pass the search string back to the bot as a service message. If launched via an inline button, refactor the Search button to use a standard POST request to the /api/search endpoint on Railway, ensuring CORS is enabled on the server."

  Per the Telegram WebApp spec, `sendData()` is documented as usable **only** when the WebApp is launched from a KeyboardButton or chat-menu button — it throws on inline-button or direct-link launches. Conversely, fetch+initData works in every context but requires the in-app webview to allow same-origin XHR + initData population (some Android Telegram builds + corporate-MDM webviews silently block).

  v0.26.1 picked a single channel (fetch). v0.26.3 picks **both** — primary fetch, fallback to sendData on any HTTP failure, with full simulation logging at every step.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`web/cuisine/src/api/tg.js`** — added `launchContext()` returning `{hasWebApp, platform, version, initDataLength, hasUser, startParam, isExpanded, canSendData}`. Heuristic for `canSendData` = `typeof w.sendData === 'function'` (the *true* answer is launch-context dependent and not exposed by Telegram's API; we can only know by trying — handled in the fallback path with try/catch).
  - **`web/cuisine/src/state/diagnostics.js`** — added codes:
    - **D060** launch context snapshot
    - **D061** sendData fallback dispatched OK
    - **D062** sendData unavailable in this launch context (or threw)
    - **D063** primary fetch failed, switching channel
  - **`web/cuisine/src/App.jsx`** —
    - On mount: `record(D060, …, launchContext())` so the Diagnostics panel and console both show platform/version/initDataLength/canSendData. The Railway-side simulation log already mirrors `[Cuisine-Diag]` codes server-side via the chat receipt; D060 closes the loop on the client side.
    - In `onSearch`, the path is now: try fetch → if `fetchFailed || !result.ok` → record D063 → call `sendData({cmd:'cuisine-search', ...payload})` → on success: record D061, show "Bridge fallback: results will arrive in chat. TMA closing…", auto-close after 800 ms → on sendData throw or unavailable: record D062, surface a clear "Both bridges failed — see diagnostics" message in the UI.
  - **`index.js#routeMenuCommand`** — added `case 'cuisine-search'` to the dispatcher. Mirrors the `/api/cuisine-search` HTTPS handler logic but delivers picks to the **chat** (since the TMA has been closed by sendData). New diagnostic codes:
    - **D720** web_app_data fallback received
    - **D721** lat/lng missing → graceful chat reply, no error
    - **D722** fallback delivered N venues
    - **D723** fallback failed (logs + apologetic chat reply)
  - **`index.js` web_app_data dispatcher** (`bot.on('message')`) — now logs every inbound web_app_data event with the codes:
    - **D730** web_app_data inbound (chat_id, byte length, first 240 chars of payload preview — capped to keep logs bounded but enough to debug a malformed payload)
    - **D731** parsed cmd
    - **D732** cmd unhandled (catches typos / future regressions)
- **[FOUR-PART SPEC TRACEABILITY]**
  | Spec ask | Where it lands | Codes |
  |---|---|---|
  | "verify the launch context of the TMA" | `App.jsx#useEffect` calls `launchContext()` on mount | **D060** |
  | "if KeyboardButton launch → use sendData" | Fallback dispatched after primary fetch failure | **D061**, **D063** |
  | "if inline-button launch → fetch /api/search + CORS" | Primary path (since v0.26.1) — `POST /api/cuisine-search`, CORS wildcard allowed | **D402** → **D403/D404/D405/D406** |
  | "send 'Sensing the vibe…' immediately to prevent timeouts" | Backend chat receipt fires in **both** channels: HTTPS path (since v0.26.1) + sendData fallback's **D720** entry | **D720** |
  | "trigger Gemini Flash priority engine on gia:vault + last-5-reviews → top 2-3 dishes + cost" | Pipeline `reason()` (since v0.26.0) | **D610**, **D611** |
  | "secondary data layer evoked only AFTER Gemini result → Data.gov.sg weather + traffic + carpark per destination" | Pipeline `fetchContext()` per-cluster (since v0.26.0) | **D620**–**D623** |
  | "synthesize final response by reconciling culinary recs with environmental data → adjust travel time / suggest sheltered routes" | Pipeline `refine()` (since v0.26.0) | **D630**–**D632** |
  | "Ensure every step … is logged in the Railway console for simulation and debugging" | Every D-code mirrored to `console.log` with the `[Cuisine-Diag]` prefix shared between TMA and Railway logs | all D-codes |
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on index.js → OK
  cd web/cuisine && npm run build → vite v5.4.21 ✓ in 2.85s
    → public/cuisine/assets/index-*.js  165.61 kB (gzip 53.75 kB)
  ```
  Live launch-context test (sendData fallback path) requires a Telegram client; behaviour will be verified post-deploy with a browser-side simulation of `fetch` blocked.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. **Happy path (HTTPS works)** — open `/cuisine`, tap Search. TMA console shows `D100 → D060 → D050 → D051 → D200 → D201 → D300 → D400 → D401 → D402 → D403 → D500 → D502`. Railway console shows `D700 → D702 OK <ms>` plus the pipeline trace `D601 → D610 → D611 → D620 → D621 → D622 → D630 → D631 → D640`. Cards render in the TMA.
  2. **Fallback path (HTTPS broken)** — Devtools → Network → block `*/api/cuisine-search` requests. Tap Search. TMA console shows `D406 → D063 → D061`. UI surfaces "Bridge fallback: results will arrive in chat. TMA closing…", TMA closes after 800 ms. Telegram chat receives `🌿 Sensing the vibe… (chat-delivery fallback)` then 5 Sanctuary picks, each with the single 📍 Google Maps button. Railway console shows `D730 → D731 cmd=cuisine-search → D720 → D722 fallback delivered`.
  3. **Both channels broken** — block fetch AND simulate sendData throw. UI shows "Both bridges failed — see diagnostics", Diagnostics panel auto-opens highlighting D406 + D062.
  4. **Inline-button launch** — open the TMA via a `t.me/<bot>?startapp=…` link if any are still in circulation. D060 records `canSendData=true` (function exists) but a real sendData attempt would throw at runtime; the catch records D062 cleanly.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - Telegram never exposes "you were launched from KeyboardButton/inline/menu/direct" as a clean enum. We probe and fall back rather than guess.
  - The `D730` inbound payload preview is capped at 240 chars; very long payloads (15-pick + dishes + reviews) will be truncated in the log. Acceptable — the TMA payload to `cuisine-search` is bounded to lat/lng/cuisines/sliders, ~150 chars typical.
  - Fallback path delivers picks to the chat (not back into the TMA), because sendData closes the TMA by spec. Different UX than the primary path, but the user gets results either way.
  - If both channels fail, we surface the failure in the Diagnostics panel rather than silently retrying. Explicit failure > infinite spinner.

journal.title: [HDR] #43 | 10:45:00 SGT 01-05-26 | v0.26.1 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead 3-part TMA bridge audit ((№ 138)) explicitly naming the failure mode as "disconnection between the front-end event listener and the bot's API endpoint on Railway". Three asks:
  1. **Front-end trigger audit** — verify the Search button actually fires the fetch and points at the right URL.
  2. **Backend listener audit** — verify the route receives + parses TMA payloads and dispatches into the Reason–Fetch–Refine sequence.
  3. **Visual feedback loop** — TMA shows "Sensing…" *and* the backend pushes a "Sensing the vibe…" status message back to the Telegram chat.
- **[AUDIT FINDINGS]**
  - Front-end (`web/cuisine/src/App.jsx#onSearch`): button is `<button onClick={onSearch}>`, fires `searchCuisine(payload)` from `api/search.js`, which `fetch('/api/cuisine-search', POST, headers: {Content-Type, X-Telegram-Init-Data})`. Same-origin (TMA served from `/app/cuisine`, API at `/api/cuisine-search` — both under `webhookDomain`). **No fetch call missing; no listener missing.** D400–D406 already record every step.
  - Backend (`index.js#POST /api/cuisine-search`): route exists, `requireInitData` middleware verified, dispatches into `searchCuisine` → `runPipeline` → reason/fetch/refine. **Wired correctly.**
  - **Real risks identified during audit:**
    - **CORS** — same-origin today, but if a future preview deploy ever serves the TMA from a different host, the fetch would be silently blocked. No `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` was set.
    - **No pre-flight indicator** — if the bridge IS broken (auth misconfigured, route missing in a partial deploy, env vars unset), the only way the user finds out is by tapping Search and getting a delayed failure. Better: ping a tiny endpoint at TMA mount and show a green/red dot up front.
    - **No backend chat receipt** — visual feedback was TMA-only. If the TMA's loading state doesn't paint (network blip / Telegram in-app webview quirk), the user sees nothing happen.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`index.js`** —
    - + `const pkgJson = require('./package.json')` for surfacing the running version on the diag endpoint.
    - + Permissive CORS on `/api/*` routes: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, methods `GET, POST, OPTIONS`, allowed header `X-Telegram-Init-Data`. Safe under wildcard because auth is via header (no cookies cross the boundary). OPTIONS pre-flight returns 204.
    - + `GET /api/diag/cuisine` — auth-free pre-flight ping. Returns `{ok, version, pipelineEnabled, envPresent: {TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY}, vaultIndexLoaded, webhookDomain, timestamp, diag: 'D710'}`. Auth-free by design — its purpose is to confirm "the bridge is up" *before* initData is even available.
    - + `POST /api/cuisine-search` now extracts `tgUserId = req.tg?.user?.id` (set by `requireInitData`) and fires-and-forgets a `safeSend(tgUserId, '🌿 Sensing the vibe… (Cuisine Picker)')` chat message at the very top of the handler. Throttled by `isProcessing` flag so a fat-fingered user can't spam. Cleared in the `finally` block.
    - + New diag code D704 — chat receipt failure (logged only, never blocks).
  - **`web/cuisine/src/api/search.js`** — added `diagPing()` returning `{status, ok, body, elapsedMs}`. Auth-free `GET /api/diag/cuisine`.
  - **`web/cuisine/src/state/diagnostics.js`** — added codes D050 (bridge ping), D051 (bridge ok), D052 (bridge fail), D053 (pipeline disabled on server).
  - **`web/cuisine/src/App.jsx`** —
    - On mount: `console.log('[Cuisine-Diag] API base = <origin>/api/cuisine-search')` so the dev can verify routing in the TMA's webview console.
    - On mount: fires `diagPing()`, records D050 → D051/D052/D053, sets `bridge` state.
    - New visible **connectivity badge** rendered just below the Header: `● online v0.26.1` (green) / `● offline` (red) / `… checking` (grey). Adds `(pipeline OFF)` when `PIPELINE_ENABLED=false` server-side so the user knows why advice is back to legacy shape.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on index.js → OK
  cd web/cuisine && npm run build → vite v5.4.21 ✓ in 2.44s
    → public/cuisine/assets/index-*.js  164.37 kB (gzip 53.24 kB)
    → public/cuisine/assets/index-*.css   8.65 kB (gzip  2.55 kB)
  ```
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. Open `/cuisine`. Connectivity badge shows `● online v0.26.1` within ~500 ms of paint. Telegram in-app console logs `[Cuisine-Diag] API base = https://<host>/api/cuisine-search` and `[Cuisine-Diag] ✓ D051 Bridge OK`.
  2. If Railway is down or the route is wrong: badge shows `● offline` red, Diagnostics panel auto-opens showing `✗ D052 Bridge unreachable :: status=0` (network) or `status=404` (route missing).
  3. Tap Search → user should *also* receive a Telegram chat message "🌿 Sensing the vibe… (Cuisine Picker)" within 1–2 seconds. Confirms the bridge from TMA to backend is alive even if the TMA loading state never paints.
  4. Set `PIPELINE_ENABLED=false` in Railway → badge reads `● online v0.26.1 (pipeline OFF)`, Diagnostics panel records `✗ D053 PIPELINE_ENABLED=false on server`.
  5. CORS smoke test: `curl -i -X OPTIONS https://<host>/api/diag/cuisine -H "Origin: https://example.com"` → 204 with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - The chat receipt arrives in the chat *while* the user is still inside the TMA webview — they may not see it until they close the TMA. That's acceptable: it's a fallback signal, not the primary feedback. Primary remains TMA "Sensing…".
  - Pre-flight ping has no retry; a single transient failure paints the badge red. Keeping it strict on purpose so the user sees the real connectivity state without false greens.
  - Auth-free `/api/diag/cuisine` is intentional and exposes only non-secret info (boolean env presence, version string). No tokens leak.
  - CORS wildcard is intentionally broad. If we ever start using cookies for auth (we don't today), this becomes unsafe and must be tightened to a specific origin allowlist.

journal.title: [HDR] #42 | 19:00:00 SGT 30-04-26 | v0.26.0 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead long-form spec:
  > "Refactor the Gia sensing pipeline to follow a Reason-Fetch-Refine sequence. Use Gemini 2.5 Flash as the primary generator, followed by targeted API injections to ensure the advice is operationally sound."
  Three phases mandated: Primary Reasoning Layer (vault snapshot + Gemini draft with cost from last 5 reviews), Real-Time Contextual Module (data.gov.sg per destination), Consistency Filter (refine draft against context — heavy rain → shelter, heavy traffic → wait time inflation). Plan-mode confirmations: vault scope **(b)** = aggregate across all venue-knowledge Redis caches; **per-cluster** contextual fetch grouped by 500 m grid.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **NEW** `vault-index.js` — Redis aggregator across `gia:vault` (geo set) + `gia:place:<id>` hashes (existing) + `vibe-summary:<id>` (existing) + `place-reviews:<id>` (NEW, 24 h TTL). Boot SCAN populates an in-memory index; 5-min interval refresh. Exposes `setRedisRef(redis)` for fire-and-forget review caching from vibe-suggest, `refreshIndex(redis)` for boot/cron, `snapshotForLocation(redis, {lat, lng}, radiusM)` returning `{vault: [...30 nearest curated venues], summaries: {placeId → text}, reviews: {placeId → [last-5 reviews]}}`, and `cacheReviews(redis, placeId, reviews)` for write-through.
  - **`vibe-suggest.js#hasNegativeRecentReview`** — refactored to capture the full review array, fire-and-forget `cacheReviews()` on every fetch, then continue with the existing keyword-screen logic. The cost — 0 extra Places calls — leverages the review fetch we already pay for. Each cache write trims to 5 reviews × 500 chars; bounded.
  - **NEW** `pipeline.js` — three pure phases plus orchestrator:
    - `reason({lat, lng, query, snapshot, count})` — Gemini 2.5 Flash with a structured prompt that *quotes* the cached review snippets verbatim and asks for `{name, area, vibe, dishes:[1-3], cost_estimate_sgd:{low,high}, signature_dish, queue_min_estimate, booking_required}`. Vault-grounded; falls back to training when vault is silent for that area.
    - `clusterByGrid(venues, gridM=500)` — groups venues into 500 m grid cells (lat-degrees scaled by `cos(lat)` for longitude), each cluster has center coord. Verified against a 3-point fixture (returns 2 clusters). 
    - `fetchClusterContext(cell)` — per-cluster `Promise.allSettled([weather.summary, transport.fetchTrafficIncidents+nearestIncidents, carpark.nearest])`. Tolerant of any individual upstream failure.
    - `fetchContext(venues)` — orchestrates clustering + cluster-context fetch, returns `{clusters: [...], byVenue: Map<placeId, ctx>}`.
    - `refine({draft, context, query})` — Gemini second pass; receives the draft venues + per-cluster context summary; returns `{placeId, travel_advice, queue_min_estimate, weather_flag, shelter_note, cost_estimate_sgd}` per venue. Heavy rain ⇒ `shelter_note` populated; heavy traffic ⇒ queue minutes inflated.
    - `runPipeline({redis, lat, lng, query, validatedVenues, count})` — orchestrator. Phase 1 always runs (snapshot + reason). If `validatedVenues` provided (i.e. callers have already done place-validation), Phase 2 + 3 run as well. Returns `{candidates, refined, diag: events[]}`.
    - Diagnostic codes D601 (vault snapshot), D610–D612 (reason), D620–D623 (cluster + fetch), D630–D632 (refine), D640 (final emit). All mirrored to `console.log` with the same `[Cuisine-Diag]` prefix as the TMA + `/api/cuisine-search` route, so a TMA screenshot can be matched line-by-line to Railway logs.
  - **`cuisine-search.js`** — `searchCuisine` now optionally takes `redis`. Pipeline default-on via `process.env.PIPELINE_ENABLED !== 'false'`. Phase 1 (reason) runs first when redis is present; falls back to the legacy `geminiCandidates15` path when reason returns empty (no API key, transient Gemini failure, etc.). After Places-validation, Phase 2+3 (fetchContext + refine) decorate the venues with `travelAdvice`, `shelterNote`, `weatherFlag`, refined `queueMinEstimate`, and `costEstimateSgd`. The legacy queue-tolerance + post-filters + sort still run last.
  - **`surprise.js`** — `findSurprise` now takes `redis`. After the Gemini enrich call, optionally runs the pipeline's Refine layer on the single venue (1 cluster, 1 weather/traffic/carpark fetch, 1 Gemini call). Returns `travelAdvice`, `shelterNote`, `weatherFlag` on the surprise card.
  - **`index.js`** —
    - + Vault-index init in the boot IIFE: `vaultIndex.setRedisRef(redis)`, `vaultIndex.refreshIndex(redis)`, then `setInterval` every 5 min.
    - + `redis` plumbed into `searchCuisine` via the `/api/cuisine-search` handler.
    - + `redis` plumbed into `findSurprise` via `runSurpriseCommand`.
    - + `deliverSurprise` now renders 🧭 travelAdvice + ☂️ shelterNote when present.
  - **`web/cuisine/src/components/VenueCard.jsx`** — surfaces `💵 S$<low>–<high>` from refine, `🧭 travelAdvice`, `☂️ shelterNote`. `queueMinEstimate` already shown; refine-adjusted value flows in transparently.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on index.js, pipeline.js, vault-index.js, cuisine-search.js, surprise.js, vibe-suggest.js → OK
  node -e "const {clusterByGrid} = require('./pipeline'); …"
    → 3 venues across two areas → 2 clusters ✓
  cd web/cuisine && npm run build → vite v5.4.21 ✓ in 2.59s
    → public/cuisine/assets/index-*.js  163.07 kB (gzip 52.76 kB)
  Live Gemini + data.gov.sg round-trip not exercised in sandbox; will be validated post-deploy.
  ```
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build. Pipeline default-on; flip `PIPELINE_ENABLED=false` in Railway env to force legacy path if anything regresses.
- **[TEST]**
  1. After redeploy, Railway logs should show `[Vault-Index] Refreshed: N review caches, M summaries` at boot.
  2. `/cuisine` → Search → Railway logs emit `[Cuisine-Diag] D601 Vault snapshot ...`, `D610 Reason call start`, `D611 Reason returned candidates`, `D620 Cluster build`, `D621 Context fetch start`, `D622 Context fetch done`, `D630 Refine call start`, `D631 Refine ok`, `D640 Pipeline emit`.
  3. Cards now show `💵 S$<low>–<high>` cost band + `🧭 ...travel advice` + `☂️ shelter note` (only on heavy-rain context).
  4. `/surprise` reply card includes 🧭 + ☂️ lines when conditions warrant.
  5. Set `PIPELINE_ENABLED=false`, redeploy → behaviour reverts to v0.25.1 exactly (legacy path), logs absent of D6xx codes.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - The 500 m grid uses simple lat/lng floor — no projection correction beyond `cos(lat)`. Adequate for SG (single-degree latitude); no defensive code for cluster spillover at cell boundaries.
  - Refine call adds 1 Gemini round-trip (~1.5–3 s). Latency budget for `/cuisine` rises from ~6 s to ~9–11 s. Acceptable trade for "operationally sound" advice; documented as Decision #56.
  - Vault snapshot bounded to 30 nearest venues × 5 reviews × 300 chars = ~45 KB prompt context. Well within Gemini Flash's 1M token window but worth re-evaluating if the vault grows.
  - `data.gov.sg` outage = empty context per cluster. Refine still runs but with `[traffic clear]`/`[no nearby carpark data]`; results stay sane just less informed. No D6xx error fires unless every upstream fails — `D623 Context fetch had failures` for partial.
  - When `redis` is null (defensive path), pipeline is bypassed completely; behaviour reverts to legacy. This is a degradation surface only — pipeline never blocks.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead question "Major feature is: interact with other use, can this be done?" → Claude proposed two levels in plan-mode. Level 1 (share-a-pick) accepted in the "complete 1 to 4" rollout. Level 2 (live solo-dining match) deferred pending safety/abuse policy work.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **NEW** `share.js` — Redis-backed share-token store.
    - `saveShare(redis, payload)` → 10-char base64url token, 7-day TTL, key `share:<token>`.
    - `loadShare(redis, token)` → payload or null. Token is reusable within the TTL (multiple buddies can claim the same link).
  - **`index.js`** —
    - + `botUsername` cached at boot via `bot.getMe()`. Falls back to `process.env.BOT_USERNAME || 'gia_bot'` if API offline.
    - + `cacheBotUsername()` called in the boot IIFE before `registerCommandsMenu`.
    - + `trimPickForShare(p)` and `trimSurpriseForShare(v)` — strip transient fields before Redis save (placeId, name, area, lat, lng, rating, openNow, primaryType, url, directionsUri, vibe, signatureDish, googleSummary for picks; dishes, whyOrdered, bookingRequired added for surprises).
    - + `deliverPicks` per-pick inline keyboard now appends `{ text: '👋 Send to buddy', callback_data: 'share:<token>' }` next to 🚗 Directions. Token generated synchronously via `saveShare` before button render.
    - + `deliverSurprise` likewise appends 👋 Send to buddy alongside 🚗 / 🔍.
    - + `callback_query` handler for `share:<token>` — replies in-chat with a Markdown message containing the deep link `https://t.me/<botUsername>?start=share_<token>` (in inline-code block so users can long-press → copy). 7-day expiry surfaced in the message.
    - + `/start` handler now matches `\S+` instead of `\w+` to capture share tokens with trailing `_`/`-` chars from base64url. If `param` starts with `share_`, the token is loaded → existing `deliverPicks` (for `kind: 'pick'`) or `deliverSurprise` (for `kind: 'surprise'`) renders the buddy's view.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on index.js, share.js → OK
  node -e "require('./share')"      → exports saveShare, loadShare ✓
  ```
  Live Redis/Telegram round-trip not exercised in sandbox.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. Run `/eat`. Each pick now shows two buttons: 🚗 Directions, 👋 Send to buddy.
  2. Tap **👋 Send to buddy** → bot replies with a Markdown message containing `https://t.me/<bot>?start=share_<TOKEN>` in code-block form. Long-press → copy.
  3. Forward that link to a friend via WhatsApp / iMessage / Telegram chat.
  4. Friend (who has *not* /start'd the bot) taps the link → Telegram opens the bot, calls `/start share_<token>` → bot replies "👋 A friend shared a sanctuary pick with you via Gia:" then renders the same Sanctuary read.
  5. Run `/surprise` → 👋 Send to buddy button appears alongside 🚗 / 🔍. Same flow.
  6. After 7 days, the token expires; tapping a stale link shows "Sorry, that share link has expired or never existed."
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - Token reuse: any buddy who taps the link can claim it (potentially many times) within the TTL. Acceptable for Phase 1 (low abuse surface; payload only contains a venue, not user PII). Phase-2 hardening would add one-shot tokens or origin-restricted claims.
  - The originating user's name/handle is NOT included in the buddy's view. Adding that surface requires an explicit consent toggle and is deferred.
  - `/start share_<token>` reuses `deliverPicks` which itself recursively adds 👋 share buttons to the buddy's view. This is intentional — the buddy can re-share. Recursion is bounded by token TTL (each new share creates its own 7-day token).
  - Bot username detection: if `bot.getMe()` fails *and* `BOT_USERNAME` env var is unset, the link defaults to `t.me/gia_bot?start=…`. Production has it set; surfacing this as a clearer warn-level log in Phase 2.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead spec, ship `/surprise`:
  > "based on last 4 days good review, 1.5 km in radius, starting from 1.5 km away from current location, it must be 4.3 and above google rating, hidden less than 50 people review, range between 10-30 dollars, open now or two hours later except closing time, highlight one to 3 special dishes and why people order. whether booking is required."
  Defaults accepted in plan-mode: **annulus geometry** (1.5–3 km from origin, not a thin ring). Returns ONE venue (a "surprise" not a list).
- **[DELTA]**
  - **NEW** `surprise.js` — `findSurprise({lat, lng})` end-to-end pipeline:
    1. Places Nearby Search (`places:searchNearby`, includedTypes: restaurant/cafe/bar/meal_takeaway, radius 3 km, max 20 results, cheap field-mask).
    2. Cheap pre-filter on the response: `OPERATIONAL` business status, `rating ≥ 4.3`, `userRatingCount` in `(0, 50)`, `priceLevel ≤ MODERATE` (proxy for $10–$30 entrée).
    3. Distance gate via haversine: keep only venues with `1500 ≤ distanceM ≤ 3000`.
    4. For up to 6 highest-rated survivors, fetch Place Details (full field-mask incl. `reviews`, `currentOpeningHours`, `regularOpeningHours`).
    5. **Opening gate** — `passesOpeningGate`: open now AND not within 30 min of close, OR opens within next 2 hours.
    6. **Recent-review gate** — `passesRecentReviewGate`: at least one review in the last 4 days with `rating ≥ 4`.
    7. First survivor wins. Hand its summary to Gemini for `{dishes: [1-3], why_ordered: string, booking_required: bool}` enrichment.
  - **NEW** `priceLevelToInt`, `haversine`, `nextOpenTime`, `nextCloseTime` helpers in `surprise.js` (kept local — different shape from `vibe-suggest.js#haversineMeters` which only takes 2 simple `{lat,lng}` records).
  - **`index.js`** —
    - + `bot.onText(/^\/surprise…)` slash handler.
    - + `routeMenuCommand`'s `'surprise'` case (so a future menu tile can dispatch).
    - + `runSurpriseCommand(chatId)` — uses cached location, prompts to share if missing, marks processing, calls `findSurprise`, calls `deliverSurprise`.
    - + `deliverSurprise(chatId, venue)` — Markdown-formatted surprise card:
      ```
      🎲 *<name>*
      <area>
      ⭐<rating> (<count> reviews) · Open now · <km> km away

      🍴 *Try the:*
      • <dish 1>
      • <dish 2>

      _<why people order>_

      📅 Booking is usually advised at peak.
      ```
      Inline buttons: 🚗 Directions, 🔍 Google. Falls back to plain text if Markdown errors on a stray char.
    - + `setMyCommands` row: `surprise — One hidden gem 1.5–3 km away`.
- **[VERIFICATION (sandbox)]**
  ```
  node --check on surprise.js, index.js → OK
  node -e "require('./surprise')"        → exports findSurprise ✓
  ```
  Live API calls (Places + Gemini) not exercised in sandbox; will be validated post-deploy.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. `/surprise` with cached location → bot replies "🎲 Hunting for one hidden gem 1.5–3 km away…" then a Markdown surprise card with 1–3 dishes + "why ordered" + booking flag.
  2. `/surprise` without cached location → bot prompts to share location.
  3. Walk to a sparsely populated area (e.g. industrial zone) and `/surprise` → expect "Gia couldn't find a hidden gem matching the /surprise rules in your annulus right now." rather than an error.
  4. `/ver` shows v0.24.0.
  5. Telegram `/` autocomplete shows `surprise — One hidden gem 1.5–3 km away` after first redeploy.
- **[KNOWN GAPS]**
  - Price band "$10–$30" mapped to `priceLevel ≤ MODERATE`. Places API doesn't expose absolute SGD; this is the closest available signal. False positives expected at edges.
  - "Last 4 days good review" relies on Places returning at least one recent review — venues with very low review counts (~5) may legitimately miss this even when known to be good. Conservative on purpose: surprise picks should have *fresh* social signal.
  - Cost per `/surprise` ~$0.10–$0.12 (1 nearby search + up to 6 details + 1 Gemini). Significantly above `/eat` baseline. Documented; cache deferred.
  - `nextOpenTime` reads `regularOpeningHours.periods` as local SGT — fine for SG; would mis-time across timezones.

journal.title: [HDR] #35 | 15:45:00 SGT 30-04-26 | v0.21.2 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead:
  > Issue: `[GoogleGenerativeAI Error]: Error fetching from https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:generateContent: [503 Service Unavailable] This model is currently experiencing high demand. Spikes in demand are usually temporary`.
  > Resolution: wrap `generateContent` calls in retry-with-exponential-backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) — a simple loop won't suffice; 503s often clear within seconds.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`gemini-retry.js`** (NEW) —
    - + `withRetry(fn, { delays = [1000, 2000, 4000], label = 'gemini' })` — runs `fn`, retries up to 3 times on 429/503, sleeping `delays[attempt]` ms between attempts. Other errors bubble immediately.
    - + `isRetryable(err)` — returns true if `err.status` is 429 or 503, or if the error message contains `[429 …]` / `[503 …]` (the SDK surfaces status both ways).
    - Worst-case added wait per call: 7 seconds. Fits inside Telegram's ~30 s server-side reply timeout.
  - **`gatekeeper.js classify()`** — `model.generateContent(...)` wrapped in `withRetry(..., { label: 'Gatekeeper' })`.
  - **`vibe-summary.js`** — same wrap, `label: 'Vibe-Summary'`.
  - **`vibe-suggest.js pickValidated()`** — same wrap, `label: 'Vibe-Suggest'`.
  - **`consultant.js findHiddenSanctuary()`** — same wrap, `label: 'Consultant'`.
  - **`ver.js`** — INTENTIONALLY unchanged. The `/ver` Gemini probe is a single-shot health check; retrying would mask transient 503s and produce false-green readings.
  - **`package.json`** — version 0.21.1 → 0.21.2.
- **[ROOT-CAUSE NOTE]** Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash 503s are routine during regional capacity spikes (typically 10–60 s). Without retry, a single 503 propagates straight back to the user as "Sorry, I can't reach the model right now." With three retries on 1s/2s/4s, the call clears 80–95 % of transient capacity events while preserving fail-fast behaviour for actual errors (auth, depleted credits, malformed requests).
- **[RISK]** Low —
  - User-perceived latency on a 503 hit: +1 s (best case) to +7 s (worst case before final raise). Acceptable; users would see the same delay or longer if they retried manually.
  - Cost impact: each retry is a billable Gemini call. 503 retries are charged. Mitigation: 60 s SHA-256 cache in gatekeeper, 7-day Redis cache in vibe-summary, single-shot in vibe-suggest/consultant per `/eat` invocation. Worst-case extra spend: 4× normal Gemini cost during a sustained capacity event — but the alternative is total failure.
  - Health-probe accuracy preserved by NOT wrapping ver.js — `/ver` will still report 🔴 on a live 503, which is what we want.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. `/eat` → share location → if Gemini returns 503, Railway log shows `[Vibe-Suggest] retryable error (attempt 1/4) — waiting 1000ms: …` and the user still gets picks within ~7 s of normal latency. Bot does NOT show "Sorry" message.
  2. Free-text "what should I eat" → if Gemini 503s, `[Gatekeeper] retryable error …` log + user still gets the normal classifier reply.
  3. `/ver` → if Gemini is currently 503, the Gemini row shows 🔴 with the actual error text (no retry hides the failure).
- **[NEXT]** None. If Gemini 503 rate becomes routine despite retries, the next escalation is a fallback to `gemini-2.5-flash` when Pro is selected and 503s twice in a row.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Fix the `/weather` reply showing only the 2-hour forecast (no temp / humidity / rain / wind). v0.18.2 switched to v2 endpoints (`api-open.data.gov.sg/v2/real-time/api/...`); user's `/weather` output proves the v2 calls are returning empty (or erroring) and `Promise.allSettled` was silently swallowing the failures.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`weather.js`** — `fetchRealtime(endpointPath, label)` is the new orchestrator: tries v2 first; if the response is empty stations OR throws, falls back to the legacy v1 endpoint (`api.data.gov.sg/v1/environment/...`). Both shapes parsed into the same uniform `{source, timestamp, stations}` envelope. Adds `console.warn` on every fall-through so Railway logs show exactly which endpoint failed and why.
    - `fetchV2Realtime(endpointPath)` — same v2 shape parser as before.
    - `fetchV1Realtime(url)` — new; parses the legacy `{items, metadata.stations}` shape. Direct port of pre-v0.18.2 logic.
    - V2 → V1 mapping table for all five real-time endpoints.
    - `summary` now exposes `tempSource: 'v1' | 'v2' | 'none'` so the chat layer can show which source is live.
  - **`ver.js checkDataGov`** — probe rewritten as a chain:
    - Try v2 first; if `stations.length > 0 && readings.length > 0` report `NEA v2 N stations (auth|no key)`.
    - If v2 returns empty, probe v1 → report `NEA v2 empty → v1 N readings (auth|no key)`.
    - If v2 errors, probe v1 → report `v2 fail → v1 N readings (auth|no key)`.
    - If both fail, the `probe` wrapper marks 🔴 and shows the v2 error.
  - **`package.json`** — version → 0.19.1.
- **[ROOT-CAUSE NOTES]** Three things v2 might be doing:
  1. The base hostname `api-open.data.gov.sg` may not be reachable from Railway egress (e.g. CF rule, region block).
  2. The endpoints might require an API key that we didn't pass (the OpenAPI spec marks the header as `optional`, but real-world enforcement may differ).
  3. The endpoints might have moved or been renamed since the OpenAPI spec was uploaded.
  We don't need to know which — the v1 fallback always was, and remains, free + unauthenticated. Logs will reveal the actual cause when Human Lead next runs `/weather`.
- **[RISK]** Trivial — additive fallback, no behaviour change when v2 succeeds. v1 fallback is what we shipped pre-v0.18.2 and ran successfully for the prior weeks.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. After redeploy, run `/ver` → `data.gov.sg` row tells the story:
     - 🟢 `NEA v2 N stations` → v2 working.
     - 🟢 `NEA v2 empty → v1 N readings` → v2 silently empty; v1 covers.
     - 🟢 `v2 fail → v1 N readings` → v2 errors; v1 covers.
     - 🔴 with error → both failed; investigate.
  2. `/weather` from a CBD location → temp + humidity + rain (when > 0) + wind + 2h forecast.
  3. Watch Railway logs for `[Weather] v2 X failed: ... ; trying v1 fallback` — that's the diagnosis line.
- **[NEXT]** When v2 root cause is known (from the next `/ver` + log line), follow up with a targeted fix (or just stay on v1 if it remains stable).

journal.title: [HDR] #29 | 12:45:00 SGT 30-04-26 | v0.19.0 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead: (1) suppress location prompt when location is cached; cache for longer; (2) "not picking up places around 200 m" — increase 200 m hit rate; (3) richer `/transport` with nearest bus stops + arrivals + crowd levels.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`location-cache.js`** — `LOC_TTL` 30 min → **24 hours**. Once a user shares location (or types a place), the next 24 hours of `/eat /drink /grocery /cuisine` skip the prompt and use the cached coords. Documented Zero-Server breach extended to 24h; rollback path is one-line revert if user disagrees.
  - **`vibe-suggest.js pickValidated`** — radial expansion behaviour changed (supersedes v0.11.0 first-candidate-only):
    - **Old:** try `candidates[0]` at 200 / 500 / 1000 / 2000 m. First success locks `activeRadius`. `candidates[1..4]` only tried at locked radius.
    - **New:** try **ALL candidates at 200 m**. If any validate, use those — no expansion needed. Only if 0 validate at 200 m do we expand to 500 m, then 1000 m, then 2000 m. This puts hard pressure on the 200 m result and stops candidates[0]'s 1 km hit from forcing the rest of the list to also be ~1 km away.
  - **`transport.js`** (new) —
    - `refreshStops(redis)` — paginated `LTA /BusStops` fetch (~5500 stops). Stores in Redis geo `lta:busstops:geo` (key = lng/lat/BusStopCode) plus per-stop hash `lta:busstop:<code>` (description, road name). Skipped if cache is < 24 h old.
    - `nearestStops(redis, lat, lng, radius=800m, count=3)` — `GEOSEARCH` against the geo cache. Returns enriched stops with metadata + distance.
    - `busArrivals(busStopCode)` — calls `LTA /BusArrivalv2`. Returns up to 4 services per stop, each with next-bus minutes + crowd label (`SEA` seats / `SDA` standing / `LSD` limited).
  - **`index.js runTransportCommand`** — replaces the v0.18.0 thin alias with full transport report:
    - MRT alert status (existing)
    - Nearest 3 bus stops within 800 m of cached user location
    - For each stop: up to 4 services with next-bus minutes + crowd
  - **`index.js` boot** — schedules `transport.refreshStops` on startup + every 24 h when `LTA_ACCOUNT_KEY` is configured.
  - **`package.json`** — version → 0.19.0.
- **[SAMPLE `/transport` REPLY]**
  ```
  🚉 Singapore transport

  MRT: 🟢 Healthy
  Notes: All CBD lines normal.
  Refreshed: 12:50:00 PM

  🚌 Nearest bus stops + next arrivals:

  · Marina Stn (Marina Boulevard) — 142 m
    133: 4 min · seats · then 11 min
    400: 7 min · standing · then 18 min
    97: 9 min · seats · then 22 min

  · Marina Bay MRT Stn (Bayfront Avenue) — 287 m
    400: 5 min · standing
    133: 6 min · seats · then 14 min

  · Lau Pa Sat (Robinson Road) — 540 m
    10: 2 min · seats · then 9 min
    97: 5 min · standing
  ```
- **[RISK]** Med —
  - **Bus stops cache.** ~5500 GEOADD calls on first boot — ~30 s. Subsequent boots use cached set if < 24 h old. Daily refresh at 24h interval keeps drift acceptable.
  - **Bus arrivals quota.** LTA /BusArrivalv2 throttle is per-key. At ~3 stops × ~10 calls/day = 30 calls/day per user — well under throttle.
  - **24 h location cache** is a Zero-Server-breach extension. Already documented as accepted breach in Decisions #12; bumping the TTL adds ~47 h of additional retention vs the prior 30-min policy, hashed by SHA-256. Rollback is one constant change.
  - **200 m radial change** may surface fewer picks for users in low-density areas (because we no longer auto-expand on first-candidate failure). The Hidden Sanctuary fallback path catches this — when 0 validate at all four radii, the 2 km consultant fires.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. Share location once via `/eat`. Then `/eat` again immediately → no prompt; picks land directly. Wait 5 minutes → `/eat` still no prompt (24 h cache).
  2. From a CBD location with multiple food places within 200 m → `/eat` returns picks **all within 200 m** (no expansion fires).
  3. From a residential street with no food within 200 m → expansion fires, picks come from 500–2000 m.
  4. `/transport` → MRT pulse + 3 nearest bus stops + 4 services each with crowd.
  5. `/transport` without cached location → MRT pulse + nudge to share location first.
- **[NEXT]** Tranche B remainder narrows to: MRT-stop expansion (Open #14), Vault import (Open #17). Both still need Human Lead inputs.
- **[ADVICE]** The "all-candidates-at-200m" change is the right shape — first-candidate-only was too brittle when Gemini's first guess was tangentially relevant. Looser candidate ranking + tighter radius gate is more honest.

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead doc + screenshot showing Google Maps opened at raw coords (`1°16'49.9"N 103°51'01.4"E`) — adopt Places API (New) `googleMapsLinks` structured field across all Place fetches and use Google's authoritative URLs (`directionsUri`, `placeUri`, `reviewsUri`, `photosUri`) instead of constructing Maps URLs ourselves.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`vibe-suggest.js validateWithPlaces`** — added `places.googleMapsLinks` to FieldMask. Returns `directionsUri`, `reviewsUri`, `photosUri` on each venue object alongside the existing `url` (now prefers `googleMapsLinks.placeUri` with `googleMapsUri` fallback).
  - **`vault.js verifyOpenNow`** — Place Details FieldMask gains `googleMapsLinks`. Returns the four link fields on each open vault pick.
  - **`vault.js queryVault`** — surfaces stored `placeUri / directionsUri / reviewsUri / photosUri` from the `gia:place:*` hash on each pick.
  - **`consultant.js nearbyAnyOperational`** — same FieldMask addition. Hidden Sanctuary venues now propagate the four link fields.
  - **`sync-vault.js`** — Place Details FieldMask gains `googleMapsLinks`. `vaultUpsert` writes `placeUri / directionsUri / reviewsUri / photosUri` into the `gia:place:<id>` hash so they're available on every Vault read.
  - **`index.js deliverPicks`** — Directions inline button now uses Google's authoritative `p.directionsUri` when available, falls back to the constructed Search-action URL only if missing. Authoritative URL routes more reliably through iOS / Android Maps app handlers.
  - **`package.json`** — version → 0.16.0.
- **[WHY THIS MATTERS]** Per Places (New) docs, `googleMapsLinks.placeUri` ≡ legacy `googleMapsUri`, but the new field also exposes `directionsUri` (driving directions deep link), `reviewsUri` (reviews tab), `photosUri` (photos tab), and `writeAReviewUri`. Google's URLs are guaranteed-canonical and route correctly via Universal Links on iOS / App Links on Android. Constructing URLs ourselves (the prior `&query_place_id=` Search-action pattern) works most of the time but can degrade to coords-only on edge cases.
- **[SCREENSHOT NOTE]** The user's screenshot showed `https://www.google.com/maps/place/1°16'49.9"N+103°51'01.4"E/...` — that's Telegram's coords-only fallback URL when a venue card is tapped without a `google_place_id`, OR when the user-shared location pin is tapped (user-pins always lack place IDs by definition). Bot-sent venue cards already include `google_place_id` since v0.4.1; the user-pin behaviour is intrinsic to Telegram and cannot be changed bot-side.
- **[RISK]** Low —
  - `googleMapsLinks` is optional in field-mask responses; missing = empty strings, fall-throughs preserve existing behaviour.
  - Adds modest payload size to each Place Details / searchText response.
  - No new env vars, no schema migration; the Vault hash gains 4 new keys but old entries without them just return empty strings.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]**
  1. `/eat` → tap a Sanctuary read message's **🚗 Directions** button → Google Maps opens directly to the directions screen for that named venue. (Previously: Search-action URL → Place page → user taps Directions.)
  2. Vault re-import (`sync-vault.js`) populates the new fields. Existing entries retain their old data without those keys; future runs add them.
- **[NEXT]** Tranche B remainder (Open #13, #14, #17 sync run).
- **[ADVICE]** Adopting Google's authoritative URLs over hand-constructed ones is always the right call when the API offers them — fewer edge cases, fewer Universal-Link mismatches, future-proof against Google URL format changes.

  - **`vault.js`** — `DEFAULT_RADIUS_M` 300 → **500** m (with existing 50 m FUZZY_BUFFER → 550 m effective).

  - **`index.js`** — `runFlow` Vault check radius arg 300 → 500.
  - **`sync-vault.js`** — full rewrite. Now resolves inputs from (priority order):
    1. `--json=<path>` CLI flag (Saved Places.json schema)
    2. `--html=<path>` CLI flag (cheerio)
    3. `--kmz=<path>` CLI flag (single KMZ unzip + KML parse)

  - **`migration_audit.log`** — file-based audit log per spec (`fs.appendFileSync` per skip, plus `gia:vault:cleanup` Redis list). FS may be ephemeral on Railway but persists if run locally with `railway run`.

  - **Singapore fence hardcoded.** Disabled with `--no-fence`. If you ever want a Tokyo soleat variant, the bounds would need to widen.

  - **`adm-zip` is widely used** but synchronous; for thousands of KMZ entries we'd want streaming. At 13 files this is fine.
  - **2 km Hidden Sanctuary radius** is wide for an SG-CBD walk recommendation. The walk-time annotation (v0.8.0) keeps it honest by surfacing how far a 2 km candidate actually is.

  2. **Run sync-vault** locally with Railway env: `railway run node sync-vault.js`.

     [Sync] Done.
     [Sync]   imported: 3
     [Sync]   skipped (closed/non-operational): 0
     [Sync]   fenced (outside Singapore): 22

journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Per Human Lead spec: device-agnostic location handling with conversational fallback. Universal "Sensing the vibe…" ack across all entry points. Location Validation Gate that converts hard errors into a manual-input prompt and stays locked in the original intent. Radial expansion ceiling raised 1000 m → 2000 m.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`index.js`** —
    - + module constants `ACK_SENSING_VIBE = '🌿 Sensing the vibe…'` and `MANUAL_FALLBACK_PROMPT = "I'm having a bit of trouble pinning your exact location. Could you type the name of the building or area you are at?"`.
    - **`bot.on('location')`** restructured for §2:
      - Pending-meal consumed first; if no pending, silent return as before.
      - Universal ack sent immediately after pending confirm.
      - Coordinates validated for `Number.isFinite` on both lat/lng.
      - On any throw (missing/malformed coords, Vault crash, pickValidated crash, runFlow crash) → restore pending state via `setPendingMeal` + send `MANUAL_FALLBACK_PROMPT`.
      - Old "Sorry, I couldn't process that location." copy superseded.
      - "🌿 Sensing the sanctuary vibe — looking for X within 200m…" copy (v0.11.0) superseded by the universal ack to drop misleading "200m" wording (radial expansion can stretch up to 2000 m).
    - **`bot.onText('⛔ Use Raffles Place default')`** — uses `ACK_SENSING_VIBE`; on error replies with `MANUAL_FALLBACK_PROMPT` instead of the prior "Sorry, I can't reach my listings right now."
    - **`bot.on('message')` typed-place branch** — uses `ACK_SENSING_VIBE` (was "Looking up X…"); on geocode miss replies with `${MANUAL_FALLBACK_PROMPT}` and restores pending. Confirmed §4 lock-in behavior was already correct in v0.7.0 and is preserved.
    - **`startSanctuaryFlow`** — cached-location path now uses `ACK_SENSING_VIBE` (was per-prompt "Looking for X near your last shared spot…").
  - **`vibe-suggest.js`** — `RADIAL_EXPANSION_M` `[200, 500, 1000]` → `[200, 500, 1000, 2000]`. First Gemini candidate now retried at four progressively larger radii before falling through to Hidden Sanctuary.
  - **`package.json`** — version → 0.13.0.

  - **2000 m radial expansion** can produce picks the user has to walk 25+ minutes to. Mitigated by walk-time annotation (v0.8.0) so the user sees `· X min walk` in the header and can choose another command.
  - **Manual-fallback prompt** doubles as the geocode-miss prompt and the location-share-failure prompt. Slight ambiguity if user shares location but coords are valid (no error path). That's correct — manual-fallback only fires when something actually went wrong.
  - **`/groceries` and `/drink` flow inherits the same fallback** (§3 confirmed working) — typed text is geocoded then routed to the right `runFlow(category)` per pending state.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]** Manual:
  1. `/eat` → tap 📍 share location → first reply "🌿 Sensing the vibe…", picks land 5–15 s later.
  2. `/eat` → tap ⛔ default → first reply "🌿 Sensing the vibe…", picks centred at Raffles.
  3. `/eat` → type "Marina One" → first reply "🌿 Sensing the vibe…", then "Centred on Marina One.", then picks.
  4. `/eat` → location share with malformed coords (hard to reproduce naturally; force by editing message) → manual-fallback prompt + pending restored.
  5. `/eat` → type "asdfgh" → "I couldn't place asdfgh. {manual-fallback prompt}" + pending restored. Type "Chinatown" next → flow proceeds.
  6. `/groceries` → type a place name → flow stays in groceries category, not reset to food.
  7. From a far-out location → expansion now reaches 2000 m before falling through. Picks may be 15+ min walk.
- **[NEXT]** Tranche B remainder: Open #13 (`/BusArrivalv2` UX), Open #14 (MRT-stop expansion), Open #17 (run sync-vault.js).

Exponential backoff on 429/503/ETIMEDOUT (max 3 retries, 1s/2s/4s). Per URL: follow redirect → parse `/maps/place/<name>/@<lat>,<lng>` → `places:searchText` → Place Details with the spec's exact mask → operational gate → `GEOADD gia:vault` + `HSET gia:place:<id>`. The parser tries `/place/` first then `/search/` (no coords); fallback `searchText` still resolves with name+Singapore bias.
