journal.title: [HDR] #6 | 23:50:00 SGT 29-04-26 | v0.4.3 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Detect whether Google Maps app is installed on iOS/iPadOS, and route the TWA "Open in Google Maps" action accordingly. v0.4.2 fixed the URL format but still relied on Universal Links picking the right destination — Human Lead's requirement is "Google Maps must be installed; detect if not."
- **[ROOT CAUSE recap]** iOS does not expose an "is X app installed?" check to webviews for privacy reasons. The standard pattern is to attempt the app's URL scheme (here `comgooglemaps://…`) and watch for the page-hidden visibility signal — if the page stays visible after a short timeout, the app didn't open.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`public/app.js`** — full rewrite of the InfoWindow link handler:
    - New helpers `isIOS()`, `externalOpen(url)`, `ask(message, callback)`, `openMapsForVenue(v)`.
    - On iOS: sets `window.location.href = 'comgooglemaps://?q=<name>&center=<lat>,<lng>&zoom=17'` and listens for `visibilitychange`. If the page goes hidden within 1500 ms, Google Maps opened — exit silently. If still visible afterwards, Google Maps app is not installed → prompt the user via `tg.showConfirm` (or `window.confirm` fallback) with two paths:
      - **OK** — open the App Store install page `https://apps.apple.com/app/google-maps/id585027354`.
      - **Cancel** — open the documented Google Maps Search-action URL `…/maps/search/?api=1&query=<name>&query_place_id=<id>` in the system browser.
    - On non-iOS: bypass the probe and open the HTTPS URL via `tg.openLink()`.
    - Click handler attached via Google Maps `info.addListener('domready', …)` per InfoWindow render — replaces the previous `domready`-querySelector pattern with a deterministic per-venue `linkId`.
  - **`package.json`** — version → 0.4.3.
- **[RISK]** Low–Medium —
  - The visibility-detection trick is well-established but can produce false negatives if iPadOS animation timing varies. Conservative 1500 ms timeout chosen.
  - `tg.showConfirm` requires Telegram WebApp 6.2+; older clients fall back to `window.confirm`, which inside a Mini App may show as a system alert (less polished but functional).
  - `comgooglemaps://` is Google Maps' documented iOS URL scheme. If they ever change it, the probe silently fails and we fall through to the install prompt — not catastrophic.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]** Human Lead on iPadOS:
  1. With Google Maps installed → tap "Open in Google Maps" → app opens directly to the named Place.
  2. (Optional, if the user has a second device without Google Maps) → tap link → install prompt appears → Cancel opens the named Place in browser.
- **[NEXT]** Phase 4 — GrabID PKCE for live quietness signal.
- **[ADVICE]** iOS Universal Links and URL schemes overlap awkwardly. Universal Links favour the OS-default Maps app (Apple Maps); URL schemes are app-specific. The hybrid here — try scheme first, fall back to documented HTTPS — is the most reliable cross-state behaviour you can get from a webview.

journal.title: [HDR] #5 | 23:30:00 SGT 29-04-26 | v0.4.2 | n/a kb | n/a lines
journal.body:
- **[INTENT]** Patch fix on top of v0.4.1. Human Lead is on iPadOS with both Google Maps and Apple Maps installed. The TWA "Open in Maps" link (InfoWindow surface #3 in the diagnostic) was still opening with raw coordinates rather than the named Place page after v0.4.1.
- **[ROOT CAUSE]** v0.4.1 used the URL pattern `https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:<id>`. iPadOS Universal Links route `https://www.google.com/maps/...` URLs to whichever Maps app the OS picks; with both Google Maps and Apple Maps installed, the link can land in Apple Maps, which does NOT understand `place_id:<id>` and degrades to coords. The pattern itself is undocumented/legacy on Google's side and not Universal-Link-stable.
- **[DELTA]**
  - **`public/app.js`** — InfoWindow link now uses Google's officially documented Maps URL Schema:
    ```
    https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=<encodedName>&query_place_id=<placeId>
    ```
    The `query=<name>` ensures the venue **name** appears in the search bar even if the OS routes to a non-Google handler. The link is rendered as a `<a href="#" data-href="…">` plus a JS click handler that calls `tg.openLink(href, { try_instant_view: false })` so Telegram's WebApp opens the URL externally rather than navigating in-place inside the Mini App webview.
  - **`package.json`** — version → 0.4.2.
- **[RISK]** Low — the new URL is the canonical Google Maps Search-action URL per `developers.google.com/maps/documentation/urls`. Behaviour:
  - Safari → Google Maps web Place sheet with venue name.
  - Google Maps app installed → Universal Link routes to the Place page.
  - Apple Maps Universal Link interception → `query=<name>` keeps the **name** in the search bar; user sees the right venue rather than coords.
- **[STATUS]** PROD — auto-deploys with the next Railway build.
- **[TEST]** Human Lead to retap the InfoWindow "Open in Maps" link on iPadOS after redeploy and confirm the destination shows the venue NAME, not raw lat/lng coords.
- **[NEXT]** Phase 4 — GrabID PKCE for live quietness signal (Register Open #6).
- **[ADVICE]** Universal Links on iOS/iPadOS are a deceptively complex layer. Whenever a webview link could land in any of {Safari, app A, app B}, prefer the documented URL schema over clever shortcuts. `query_place_id` is the contract; everything else is best-effort.

sections.heading: 3. Working Style
sections.body:
| # | Observation | First seen | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Terse, quote-forward**. Provides operator-INTENT verbatim, often with screenshot context, and expects the response to lead with what changed, not how it changed. Bullet lists preferred over prose. | early arc | stable |
| 2 | **Recurring-bug stamina**. Will re-surface the same defect across multiple sessions until the upstream source is found (e.g. `[object Object]` across v0.60.154 / .155 / .156). Doesn't accept "we added more guards" if the next screenshot still shows the bug. | v0.60.154 | stable |
| 3 | **Decisive at decision-points**. When given an `AskUserQuestion` with 2–4 options, picks one (often "Option D / both") and moves on; rarely re-litigates a decided rule. | full arc | stable |
| 4 | **Per-PR doc cadence enforcer**. Codified as a standing rule (D-120) that the Journal must be updated *after opening AND after merging* every substantive PR. The Feature / Technical / Register / Vault catch-up is allowed to lag (operator pattern is end-of-arc catch-ups, not per-PR) but never the Journal. | v0.60.144 | stable |
| 5 | **Owner-only / hidden-command preference**. Diagnostic + admin surfaces stay off `setMyCommands` and behind `isOwnerChat` (`/oversight`, `/ver`, `/ftlog`); accessible to the operator but not advertised. | v0.60.142 | stable |
| 6 | **Two-locale parity expected on user-facing copy**. Every new UI string lands in EN + FR in the same PR; never "FR can wait". | early arc | stable |
| 7 | **Accepts mid-arc deferrals if logged**. Sees `[KNOWN GAPS]` + `DF-NN` entries as legitimate work breaks; will follow up on them in a quiet pass without re-asking. | full arc | stable |
| 8 | **`Status cold!` — clean-cut session boundaries**. Uses the explicit `Status cold!` cue to mark a session as logically closed (vs `Status warm` mid-arc). Future Claude sessions on the same project should treat a `Status cold!` predecessor as fully-flushed: no carryover assumptions. | observed via Journal frontmatter across v0.60.142–.149 | stable |

dashboard.body: ## Summary Catches the build Journal up to current (journal-0_60_144 entry #109 covering PRs #379–#381) and adds a repo-root CLAUDE.md codifying the operator's standing rule: after opening a PR and after it merges, record it in doc/Journal/, bump doc/.serial-state.yml, flag any due Feature/Technical/Register/vault catch-up, and refresh doc/VibeCodingRecord/. dashboard.title: v0.60.145 — Cuisine TMA: /api/cuisine/copy-all bot.sendMessage try/catch + plain-text retry; tolerate null mapUrl
dashboard.body: ## Summary — PR-A of 3 (Cuisine TMA hardening arc) First of three sequenced PRs. Fixes the recurring 'Couldn't send to chat' error on /cuisine Copy-all by wrapping both bot.sendMessage calls in try/catch with a plain-text retry (strip <b>, unescape entities), and tolerating buildMapHashUrl=null gracefully (drop the inline map button + append a Map unavailable footer). 5 new tests.

dashboard.title: v0.60.146 — Cuisine TMA: 80-cap session clipboard + ⇠ Prev FAB + multi-cuisine variant escalation (PR-B of 3)
dashboard.body: ## Summary — PR-B of 3. Three root causes addressed together. Multi-cuisine variant escalation now works. Silent fallback replaced. 80-cap session clipboard + ⇠ Prev FAB. Operator's 'stuck on the same list after 3–4 clicks' + 'back FAB' asks.

dashboard.title: v0.60.147 — Cuisine TMA: Michelin full LLM-narrate parity (vibe + whatToOrder) (PR-C of 3)
dashboard.body: ## Summary — PR-C of 3. Michelin cards now match cuisine-chip cards: curated Michelin badge + restaurantType + dishes + recentReview + vibe + signatureDish. New pipeline.narrateMichelinVenues (narrate-only LLM helper).

dashboard.title: v0.60.148 — Cuisine TMA: ⇠ Prev FAB visibility fix + /clipboard alias
dashboard.body: ## Summary. ⇠ Prev FAB was nested inside the in-strip pagination row (gated totalPages > 1 — never true for 12-venue responses) → effectively invisible. Moved to the floating FAB column. Plus /clipboard added as a /clip regex alias.

dashboard.title: v0.60.149 — Cuisine TMA: Michelin batch 40→12 + /clipboard menu entry + post-80 ↻ Recycle button
dashboard.body: ## Summary. sliceCap 40→12 fixes the first-Michelin-tap timeout. /clipboard added to the Telegram /-autocomplete menu (EN + FR). Post-80 ↻ Recycle button in lieu of close-and-reopen friction. cuisine-session.recordPage gains opts.skipCap so Michelin walks all ~130 curated entries without the 80-cap. (Merged via the GitHub web UI while the MCP server was disconnected.)

dashboard.title: v0.60.149 follow-up — Michelin remaining-count indicator + LLM dish-name guard rail
dashboard.body: ## Summary. Two refinements on top of #388. Michelin walk-through banner '📚 Curated Michelin list — N more to explore (T in total). Tap ▶ for the next batch of 12.' Plus a stripDishVerbs regex defense so the LLM's 'Order the brisket' phrasings never render as 'Try · Order the brisket'.

dashboard.title: v0.60.150 — Cuisine TMA: parallelize Michelin Places lookups + 24-h Redis cache + axios 6s→4s (the 'later Michelin' HTTP 502 fix)
dashboard.body: ## Summary. Later Michelin ▶ taps returned HTTP 502 from Railway. Root cause: 12 × Places searchText in a serial for-await loop, each 6s timeout = 72s worst case. Three coupled fixes: parallelize via Promise.allSettled; 24-h michelin:place:<slug> Redis cache (with negative-cache marker); per-call axios timeout 6s → 4s. Plus a [Michelin] handler ms=… warn log when ms > 10000.

dashboard.title: v0.60.151 — /clipboard per-clip controls: 📋 Copy (plain text) + ✏️ Rename + 🗑 Remove
dashboard.body: ## Summary. Each /clipboard row now has 4 actions: 📤 Resend (existing), 📋 Copy as plain text, ✏️ Rename (Telegram force_reply prompt), 🗑 Remove (confirm gate + Redis LSET sentinel + LREM 1 sentinel). clip-store.js gains removeClip + renameClip. 8 new tests.

dashboard.title: v0.60.152 — distance gate: PR #125's 80 km → 120 km (cuisine TMA + chat free-text)
dashboard.body: ## Summary. Two coupled constant bumps so /cuisine and /s agree on reach. index.js:9227 <= 80000 → <= 120000 (PR #125's hard gate). free-text-search.js MAX_DISTANCE_M 80000 → 120000. The JB formattedAddress filter still pins JB-mode results to Johor Bahru.

dashboard.title: v0.60.153 — Michelin: dedup fix (drop radius from criteriaHash) + force-warm enrichment cache + 'Curating' UI copy
dashboard.body: ## Summary. Three coupled Michelin fixes. (1) Drop radius from the Michelin criteriaHash — TMA slider drift was changing the hash → 'same first 12' bug. (2) New michelin:enrich:<slug> Redis cache (7-day TTL); five-step enrichment flow guarantees dishes.length ≥ 2 + non-empty recentReview on every venue. (3) 'Curating the Michelin list' loadingHint (EN + FR) replaces the generic 'Loading…' for Michelin searches.
